sentences.zh: 資治通鑑第230卷

translations.literal: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 230.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 230.

sentences.zh: 【唐紀四十六】起閼逢困敦二月，盡四月，不滿一年。

translations.literal: [Tang Annals 46] From the second month of the jiazi cycle year through the fourth month—less than a full year.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Annals 46] From the second month through the fourth month of this jiazi year—less than a full year's span.

sentences.zh: 德宗神武聖文皇帝五興元元年（

translations.literal: The fifth year of Emperor Dezong, the Divinely Martial and Sagely Literate Emperor—Xingyuan year 1 (
translations.idiomatic: Year 1 of Xingyuan, reign of Emperor Dezong, the Divinely Martial and Sagely Literate Emperor (

sentences.zh: 甲子，公元七八四年）

translations.literal: jiazi, corresponding to 784 CE)
translations.idiomatic: jiazi [784 CE])

sentences.zh: 二月，戊申，詔贈段秀實太尉，謚曰忠烈，厚恤其家。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day wushen, an edict posthumously granted Duan Xiushi the title Grand Mentor, with the posthumous name Zhonglie, and generous relief for his family.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the wushen day, the throne posthumously honored Duan Xiushi as Grand Mentor, gave him the posthumous name Zhonglie, and provided generous support for his household.

sentences.zh: 時賈隱林已卒，贈左僕射，賞其能直言也。

translations.literal: At this time Jia Yinlin had already died; he was posthumously granted Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, rewarding his ability to speak frankly.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yinlin had died by then; he too was posthumously made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, in recognition of his forthright counsel.

sentences.zh: 李希烈將兵五萬圍寧陵，引水灌之。

translations.literal: Li Xilie led fifty thousand troops to besiege Ningling and diverted water to flood it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xilie marched fifty thousand men against Ningling and had the city flooded by diverting water against its walls.

sentences.zh: 濮州刺史劉昌以三千人守之。

translations.literal: Liu Chang, prefect of Puzhou, defended it with three thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chang, the prefect of Puzhou, held the place with three thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 滑州刺史李澄密遣使請降，上許以澄為汴滑節度使。

translations.literal: Li Cheng, prefect of Huazhou, secretly sent envoys to request surrender; the emperor promised to appoint Cheng military commissioner of Bian and Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cheng, prefect of Huazhou, secretly sent envoys to offer his surrender, and the emperor agreed to make him military commissioner of Bian and Hua.

sentences.zh: 澄猶外事希烈。

translations.literal: Cheng still outwardly served Xilie.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng still maintained outward allegiance to Xilie.

sentences.zh: 希烈疑之，遣養子六百人戍白馬，召澄共攻寧陵。

translations.literal: Xilie grew suspicious of him, sent six hundred adopted sons to garrison Baima, and summoned Cheng to join in attacking Ningling.
translations.idiomatic: Suspicious of Cheng, Xilie posted six hundred of his adopted sons at Baima and ordered Cheng to join the assault on Ningling.

sentences.zh: 澄至石柱，使其眾陽驚，燒營而遁。

translations.literal: When Cheng reached Shizhu, he had his troops feign alarm, burned the camp, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: At Shizhu, Cheng had his men feign panic, burned the camp, and slipped away.

sentences.zh: 又諷養子令剽掠，澄悉收斬之，以白希烈，希烈無以罪也。

translations.literal: He also incited the adopted sons to plunder; Cheng seized and executed them all, reported this to Xilie, and Xilie had no grounds to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: He also prompted the adopted sons to loot; Cheng rounded them up and executed them, then reported the matter to Xilie, who could find no fault with him.

sentences.zh: 劉昌守寧陵，凡四十五日不釋甲。

translations.literal: Liu Chang defended Ningling for forty-five days without doffing his armor.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chang held Ningling for forty-five days without once taking off his armor.

sentences.zh: 韓滉遣其將王棲曜將兵助劉洽拒希烈，棲曜以強弩數千游汴水，夜，入寧陵城。

translations.literal: Han Huang sent his general Wang Qiyao with troops to aid Liu Qia against Xilie; Qiyao took several thousand powerful crossbows along the Bian River and by night entered Ningling.
translations.idiomatic: Han Huang sent his general Wang Qiyao to reinforce Liu Qia against Xilie; Qiyao moved several thousand heavy crossbows along the Bian River and entered Ningling by night.

sentences.zh: 明日，從城上射希烈，及其坐幄。

translations.literal: The next day, from atop the wall they shot at Xilie and struck the canopy where he sat.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they shot from the walls at Xilie and hit the canopy over his seat.

sentences.zh: 希烈驚曰：「宣、潤弩手至矣！」

translations.literal: Xilie cried in alarm, "The crossbowmen of Xuan and Run have arrived!"
translations.idiomatic: Xilie exclaimed in alarm, "The crossbowmen from Xuan and Run are here!"

sentences.zh: 遂解圍去。

translations.literal: and thereupon lifted the siege and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: And at once he broke off the siege and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 朱泚既自奉天敗歸，李晟謀取長安。

translations.literal: After Zhu Ci had returned defeated from Fengtian, Li Sheng planned to recover Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhu Ci retreated in defeat from Fengtian, Li Sheng set out to recover Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 劉德信與晟俱屯東渭橋，不受晟節制。

translations.literal: Liu Dexin was encamped with Sheng at East Wei Bridge but did not accept Sheng's command.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dexin was stationed with Sheng at East Wei Bridge but refused to submit to his authority.

sentences.zh: 晟因德信至營中，數以滬澗之敗及所過剽掠之罪，斬之。

translations.literal: When Dexin came to camp, Sheng took the occasion to enumerate his crimes—the defeat at Hujian and the plundering along his route—and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng seized the occasion when Dexin came to camp to charge him with the defeat at Hujian and with the looting along his march, and had him beheaded.

sentences.zh: 因以數騎馳入德信軍，勞其眾，無敢動者，遂並將之，軍勢益振。

translations.literal: Then with a few horsemen he galloped into Dexin's army, addressed the troops, and none dared stir; he thereupon absorbed the force, and his army's momentum grew stronger.
translations.idiomatic: He then rode into Dexin's camp with only a few horsemen, reassured the men, and none stirred against him; he absorbed the command at once, and his army's strength swelled.

sentences.zh: 李懷光既脅朝廷逐盧杞等，內不自安，遂有異志。

translations.literal: After Li Huaiguang had coerced the court into banishing Lu Qi and others, he felt ill at ease within and henceforth harbored disloyal designs.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huaiguang, having forced the court to remove Lu Qi and the others, grew uneasy in his own mind and began to turn disloyal.

sentences.zh: 又惡李晟獨當一面，恐其成功，奏請與晟合軍。

translations.literal: He also resented Li Sheng's holding an independent front alone and, fearing his success, memorialized asking to unite their armies.
translations.idiomatic: He also resented Li Sheng's independent command and, fearing his success, asked that their armies be combined.

sentences.zh: 詔許之。

translations.literal: An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 晟與懷光會於咸陽西陳濤斜，築壘未畢，泚眾大至，晟謂懷光曰：「賊若固守宮苑，或曠日持久，未易攻取。

translations.literal: Sheng and Huaiguang met west of Xianyang at Chantaoxie; before their ramparts were finished, Ci's forces arrived in strength. Sheng said to Huaiguang, "If the rebels hold fast within the palace precincts, the campaign may drag on for days and will not be easy to take.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng joined Huaiguang west of Xianyang at Chantaoxie; their ramparts were not yet finished when Ci's army came up in force. Sheng told Huaiguang, "If the rebels shut themselves inside the palace grounds, the siege may drag on and will not be easy to win.

sentences.zh: 今去其巢穴，敢出求戰，此天以賊賜明公，不可失也！」

translations.literal: Now they have left their nest and dare come out to give battle—Heaven is handing the rebels to you, my lord; this chance must not be lost!"
translations.idiomatic: They have left their lair and dare meet us in the open—Heaven is delivering the enemy into your hands; we must not let this pass!"

sentences.zh: 懷光曰：「軍適至，馬未秣，士未飯，豈可遽戰邪！」

translations.literal: Huaiguang said, "The army has only just arrived; the horses are unfed and the men have not eaten—how can we fight at once!"
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang replied, "The army has only just come up—the horses are unfed and the men unfed. How can we fight so soon!"

sentences.zh: 晟不得已乃就壁。

translations.literal: Sheng had no choice but to take to the ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng had no choice but to fall back behind the walls.

sentences.zh: 晟每與懷光同出軍，懷光軍士多掠人牛馬，晟軍秋毫不犯。

translations.literal: Whenever Sheng marched out with Huaiguang, Huaiguang's soldiers often seized people's cattle and horses, while Sheng's army would not touch so much as a blade of grass.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever they marched out together, Huaiguang's men looted cattle and horses freely, while Sheng's troops would not take even a straw.

sentences.zh: 懷光軍士惡其異己，分所獲與之，晟軍終不敢受。

translations.literal: Huaiguang's soldiers resented their difference from the rest and shared their spoils with them, but Sheng's men never dared accept.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang's soldiers resented the contrast and tried to share their loot with Sheng's men, who would never accept it.

sentences.zh: 懷光屯咸陽累月，逗留不進。

translations.literal: Huaiguang remained encamped at Xianyang for months, tarrying without advancing.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang lingered at Xianyang for months without advancing.

sentences.zh: 上屢遣中使趣之，辭以士卒疲弊，且當休息觀釁。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly sent palace envoys to urge him on; he pleaded that the troops were worn out and that they should rest and watch for an opening.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor repeatedly sent palace envoys to hurry him forward; he pleaded exhausted troops and the need to rest and watch for an opening.

sentences.zh: 諸將數勸之攻長安，懷光不從，密與朱泚通謀，事跡頗露。

translations.literal: The generals repeatedly urged an assault on Chang'an, but Huaiguang would not comply; he secretly communicated with Zhu Ci, and the signs became fairly plain.
translations.idiomatic: The generals repeatedly urged an attack on Chang'an, but Huaiguang refused; he was secretly in contact with Zhu Ci, and the signs grew plain.

sentences.zh: 李晟屢奏，恐其有變，為所並，請移軍東渭橋。

translations.literal: Li Sheng memorialized repeatedly, fearing a sudden turn and absorption into Huaiguang's command, and asked to move his army to East Wei Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng memorialized again and again, fearing treachery and absorption into Huaiguang's command, and asked to shift his army to East Wei Bridge.

sentences.zh: 上猶冀懷光革心，收其力用，寢晟奏不下。

translations.literal: The emperor still hoped Huaiguang would reform his heart and lend his strength, and shelved Sheng's memorial without acting.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still hoped to win Huaiguang back and use his strength, and set Sheng's memorial aside without acting on it.

sentences.zh: 懷光欲緩戰期，且激怒諸軍，奏言：「諸軍糧賜薄，神策獨厚，厚薄不均，難以進戰。」

translations.literal: Huaiguang wished to delay the campaign and also to inflame the other armies; he memorialized, "The grain allowances of the various armies are meager while the Shence Army alone is favored; with such uneven treatment, it is hard to advance to battle."
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang wished to stall the campaign and stir resentment among the other armies; he memorialized, "The other armies receive thin rations while the Shence alone is favored—such inequality makes united action impossible."

sentences.zh: 上以財用方窘，若糧賜皆比神策，則無以給之，不然，又逆懷光意，恐諸軍觖望。

translations.literal: The emperor, with finances already strained, saw that if all armies were paid like the Shence there would be no means to supply them; yet otherwise he would go against Huaiguang's wish and feared discontent among the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Finances were already strained: matching every army to the Shence would be impossible, yet refusing would anger Huaiguang and risk discontent in the ranks.

sentences.zh: 乃遣陸贄詣懷光營宣慰，因召李晟參議其事。

translations.literal: He therefore sent Lu Zhi to Huaiguang's camp to announce consolation and summoned Li Sheng to deliberate on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Lu Zhi to Huaiguang's camp on a mission of reassurance and summoned Li Sheng to join the deliberation.

sentences.zh: 懷光意欲晟自乞減損，使失士心，沮敗其功，乃曰：「將士戰鬥同而糧賜異，何以使之協力！」

translations.literal: Huaiguang intended that Sheng himself should ask for a reduction, thereby losing the hearts of his troops and thwarting his achievements; he said, "Officers and men fight alike yet receive different allowances—how can they be made to work together!"
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang hoped Sheng would volunteer a cut in his men's rations, lose their loyalty, and see his success undone; he said, "Men who fight side by side cannot be expected to fight as one when their pay differs!"

sentences.zh: 贄未有言，數顧晟。

translations.literal: Zhi had not yet spoken and repeatedly glanced at Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi said nothing and glanced repeatedly at Sheng.

sentences.zh: 晟曰：「公為元帥，得專號令；

translations.literal: Sheng said, "You are commander-in-chief and may issue orders as you see fit;
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said, "You are supreme commander and may issue orders as you please;

sentences.zh: 晟將一軍，受指蹤而已。

translations.literal: I command one army and merely follow your direction.
translations.idiomatic: I lead one army and follow your direction alone.

sentences.zh: 至於增減衣食，公當裁之。」

translations.literal: As for increasing or reducing food and clothing, that is for you to decide."
translations.idiomatic: As for increasing or cutting rations and clothing, that is yours to decide."

sentences.zh: 懷光默然，又不欲自減之，遂止。

translations.literal: Huaiguang fell silent; unwilling to reduce his own men's share, he let the matter drop.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang fell silent; unwilling to cut his own men's allowances, he dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 時上遣崔漢衡詣吐蕃發兵，吐蕃相尚結贊言：「蕃法發兵，以主兵大臣為信。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor sent Cui Hanheng to the Tibetans to summon troops; the Tibetan minister Shang Jiezan said, "By Tibetan law, troops are sent on the faith of the chief minister who commands the army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had sent Cui Hanheng to Tibet to request troops; the Tibetan minister Shang Jiezan said, "By our law, we march only on the word of the chief commander named in the edict.

sentences.zh: 今制書無懷光署名，故不敢進。」

translations.literal: The present imperial document bears no signature of Huaiguang, so we dare not advance."
translations.idiomatic: This edict bears no signature from Huaiguang, so we dare not march."

sentences.zh: 上命陸贄諭懷光，懷光固執以為不可，曰：「若克京城，吐蕃必縱兵焚掠，誰能遏之！

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Lu Zhi to persuade Huaiguang; Huaiguang stubbornly held it impossible and said, "If the capital is taken, the Tibetans will surely let their troops burn and plunder—who can restrain them!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Lu Zhi to persuade Huaiguang, but Huaiguang refused outright: "If we take the capital, the Tibetans will surely burn and loot—who can stop them!

sentences.zh: 此一害也。

translations.literal: This is the first harm.
translations.idiomatic: That is the first danger.

sentences.zh: 前有敕旨，募士卒克城者人賞百緡，彼發兵五萬，若援敕求賞，五百萬緡何從可得！

translations.literal: There was an earlier edict promising a reward of one hundred strings of cash to each soldier who took the city; if they send fifty thousand men and claim the reward by that edict, whence are five million strings to come!
translations.idiomatic: An earlier edict promised one hundred strings of cash to every soldier who helped take the city; if they send fifty thousand men and claim that reward, where will five million strings of cash come from!

sentences.zh: 此二害也。

translations.literal: This is the second harm.
translations.idiomatic: That is the second danger.

sentences.zh: 虜騎雖來，必不先進，勒兵自固，觀我兵勢，勝則從而分功，敗則從而圖變，譎詐多端，不可親信，此三害也。」

translations.literal: Though the barbarian cavalry may come, they will surely not advance first; they will hold their troops in readiness, watch our military strength, share the credit if we win and plot change if we lose—treacherous in many ways and not to be trusted. This is the third harm."
translations.idiomatic: Even if their horsemen come, they will not fight first; they will hold their men back, watch our strength, share the glory if we win and turn treacherous if we lose—too cunning to trust. That is the third danger."

sentences.zh: 竟不肯署敕。

translations.literal: In the end he refused to sign the edict.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he would not sign the edict.

sentences.zh: 尚結贊亦不進兵。

translations.literal: Shang Jiezan likewise did not advance his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Jiezan likewise sent no troops.

sentences.zh: 陸贄自咸陽還，上言：「賊泚稽誅，保聚宮苑，勢窮援絕，引日偷生。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi returned from Xianyang and memorialized, "The rebel Ci awaits execution, holding the palace precincts; his strength is spent and his aid cut off, prolonging his days in stolen life.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from Xianyang, Lu Zhi memorialized, "The rebel Ci clings to the palace grounds with his strength spent and his allies gone, stealing day by day to survive.

sentences.zh: 懷光總仗順之師，乘制勝之氣，鼓行芟翦，易若摧枯，而乃寇奔不追，師老不用，諸帥每欲進取，懷光輒沮其謀，據茲事情，殊不可解，陛下意在全護，委曲聽從，觀其所為，亦未知感。

translations.literal: Huaiguang commands the armies of righteousness and rides the momentum of assured victory; to march forward and mow them down should be as easy as breaking dry wood—yet when the rebels flee he does not pursue, his army grows weary and idle, and whenever the commanders wish to advance, Huaiguang thwarts their plans. Judging by these facts, it is deeply puzzling; Your Majesty has sought to protect him entirely and yielded to him in every detail, yet judging by his conduct, one cannot tell that he is grateful.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang commands the loyal armies and holds every advantage; to sweep forward and cut the rebels down should be as easy as snapping dry wood—yet when the enemy flees he will not pursue, his army grows stale, and whenever the other commanders urge an advance he blocks them. By these signs his conduct is inexplicable; Your Majesty has sheltered him at every turn, yet nothing in his actions shows gratitude.

sentences.zh: 若不別務規略，漸思制持，惟以姑息求安，終恐變故難測。

translations.literal: If we do not pursue a separate strategy and gradually devise means of control, seeking only temporary peace through indulgence, we shall ultimately fear unforeseen upheaval.
translations.idiomatic: Unless we adopt a separate strategy and begin to restrain him, seeking only peace through indulgence will end in disaster we cannot foresee.

sentences.zh: 此誠事機危迫之秋也，固不可以尋常容易處之。

translations.literal: This is truly a season when the situation is critically urgent and cannot be handled with ordinary ease.
translations.idiomatic: This is a moment of grave urgency and cannot be treated as an ordinary affair.

sentences.zh: 今李晟奏請移軍，適遇臣銜命宣慰，懷光偶論此事，臣遂泛問所宜。

translations.literal: Now Li Sheng has memorialized asking to move his army; it happened that I was charged with a mission of consolation, and Huaiguang happened to discuss this matter, so I broadly asked what he thought fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng has now asked to move his army; on my mission of reassurance to Huaiguang's camp he happened to raise the matter, and I asked in general terms what he thought best.

sentences.zh: 懷光乃云：『李晟既欲別行，某亦都不要藉。』

translations.literal: Huaiguang then said, 'Since Li Sheng wishes to march separately, I have no need of him at all.'
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang said, 'If Li Sheng wants to go his own way, I want nothing from him.'

sentences.zh: 臣猶慮有翻覆，因美其軍盛強。

translations.literal: I still feared he might change his mind and therefore praised the strength of his army.
translations.idiomatic: I still feared he might change his mind and praised the strength of his army.

sentences.zh: 懷光大自矜誇，轉有輕晟之意。

translations.literal: Huaiguang greatly prided himself and came to look down on Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang swelled with pride and began to slight Sheng.

sentences.zh: 臣又從容問云：『回日，或聖旨顧問事之可否，決定何如？』

translations.literal: I then asked at ease, 'When I return, if His Majesty inquires whether the matter may proceed, what is your final decision?'
translations.idiomatic: I then asked gently, 'When I return, if His Majesty asks whether this may proceed, what is your final word?'

sentences.zh: 懷光已肆輕言，不可中變，遂云：『恩命許去，事亦無妨。』

translations.literal: Huaiguang had already spoken lightly and could not change midway; he therefore said, 'If the gracious command permits his departure, the matter is also without harm.'
translations.idiomatic: Having spoken so freely, Huaiguang could not retract; he said, 'If the throne permits him to go, there is no objection.'

sentences.zh: 要約再三，非不詳審，雖欲追悔，固難為辭。

translations.literal: The agreement was made again and again and was not lacking in care; even if he wished to regret it, he would find it hard to find words.
translations.idiomatic: The pledge was repeated and explicit; even if he wished to take it back, he would find it hard to explain away.

sentences.zh: 伏望即以李晟表出付中書，敕下依奏，別賜懷光手詔，示以移軍事由。

translations.literal: I humbly hope Your Majesty will at once release Li Sheng's memorial to the Secretariat, issue an edict approving it as submitted, and separately bestow on Huaiguang a handwritten edict explaining the reason for the troop transfer.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to send Li Sheng's memorial to the Secretariat at once, approve it by edict, and separately send Huaiguang a handwritten edict explaining why the troops are moving.

sentences.zh: 其手詔大意云：『昨得李晟奏，請移軍城東以分賊勢。

translations.literal: The gist of the handwritten edict should read: 'Yesterday we received Li Sheng's memorial asking to move his army east of the city to divide the rebels' strength.
translations.idiomatic: The handwritten edict should say in substance: 'Yesterday Li Sheng memorialized asking to move east of the city to divide the rebel strength.

sentences.zh: 朕本欲委卿商量，適會陸贄回奏雲，見卿語及於此，仍言許去事亦無妨，遂敕本軍允其所請。』

translations.literal: We originally wished to entrust the matter to you for consultation; it happened that Lu Zhi returned reporting that he heard you speak of this and also said that permitting his departure would be without harm, whereupon we ordered his army to grant his request.'
translations.idiomatic: We meant to consult you first; Lu Zhi has just reported that you discussed this and said his departure would do no harm, so we have ordered his army to grant the request.'

sentences.zh: 如此，則詞婉而直，理順而明，雖蓄異端，何由起怨！」

translations.literal: In this way the words are gentle yet direct and the reasoning orderly and clear; even if he harbors other designs, how could resentment arise!"
translations.idiomatic: Thus the wording is courteous yet clear and the logic plain; even if he harbors other designs, how can he take offense!"

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 晟自咸陽結陳而行，歸東渭橋。

translations.literal: Sheng formed ranks at Xianyang and marched, returning to East Wei Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng drew up his ranks at Xianyang and marched back to East Wei Bridge.

sentences.zh: 時鄜坊節度使李建徽、神策行營節度使楊惠元猶與懷光聯營，陸贄復上奏曰：「懷光當管師徒，足以獨制凶寇，逗留未進，抑有它由。

translations.literal: At this time Li Jianhui, military commissioner of Bin and Fang, and Yang Huiyuan, military commissioner of the Shence field headquarters, were still encamped with Huaiguang. Lu Zhi memorialized again, "Huaiguang ought to command the armies and be sufficient alone to subdue the fierce rebels; his lingering without advancing surely has another cause.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jianhui of Bin-Fang and Yang Huiyuan of the Shence field command were still in camp with Huaiguang. Lu Zhi memorialized again: "Huaiguang should be strong enough to subdue the rebels alone; his delay must have another cause.

sentences.zh: 所患太強，不資傍助。

translations.literal: The worry is that he is too strong and needs no outside aid.
translations.idiomatic: The trouble is that he is already too strong and needs no help.

sentences.zh: 比者又遣李晟、李建徽、楊惠元三節度之眾附麗其營，無益成功，只足生事。

translations.literal: Lately we have also attached the forces of the three commissioners Li Sheng, Li Jianhui, and Yang Huiyuan to his camp; this does not help success and only breeds trouble.
translations.idiomatic: We have lately attached the armies of Li Sheng, Li Jianhui, and Yang Huiyuan to his camp—this helps victory not at all and only breeds trouble.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 四軍接壘，群帥異心，論勢力則懸絕高卑，據職名則不相統屬。

translations.literal: Four armies stand camp to camp; the commanders' hearts differ; in strength they are vastly unequal in rank, and by office they do not belong to one chain of command.
translations.idiomatic: Four armies stand cheek by jowl while their commanders pull in different directions; in power they stand far apart in rank, and by office they answer to no single chain of command.

sentences.zh: 懷光輕晟等兵微位下而忿其制不從心，晟等疑懷光養寇蓄奸而怨其事多陵己。

translations.literal: Huaiguang looks down on Sheng and the others for their small forces and low rank and resents that their command does not follow his will; Sheng and the others suspect Huaiguang of harboring the rebels and storing treachery and resent his many encroachments on themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang despises Sheng and the others for their small armies and low rank and resents their refusal to obey him; they suspect him of coddling the rebels and resent his many slights.

sentences.zh: 端居則互防飛謗，欲戰則遞恐分功，齟齬不和，嫌釁遂構，俾之同處，必不兩全。

translations.literal: At rest they guard against each other's slanders; when they wish to fight, each in turn fears sharing the credit. Discord and ill will build; if made to dwell together, both cannot survive.
translations.idiomatic: In camp they trade slanders; when battle is proposed each fears the other will steal the credit. Friction breeds suspicion, and if they remain together both cannot survive.

sentences.zh: 強者惡積而後亡，弱者勢危而先覆，覆亡之禍，翹足可期！

translations.literal: The strong, with hatred accumulated, perish afterward; the weak, in perilous straits, are overthrown first—the calamity of ruin may be expected at the lift of a foot!
translations.idiomatic: The strong will perish once hatred has piled up; the weak will fall first in their peril—disaster waits on tiptoe!

sentences.zh: 舊寇未平，新患方起，憂歎所切，實堪疚心。

translations.literal: The old foe is not yet pacified while a new peril rises; what grieves and sighs the heart is truly cause for remorse.
translations.idiomatic: The old enemy is not yet subdued and a new danger rises—this is a grief that cuts to the heart.

sentences.zh: 太上消慝於未萌，其次救失於始兆。

translations.literal: The highest course is to dispel evil before it sprouts; next is to remedy error at the first sign.
translations.idiomatic: The wisest ruler removes trouble before it sprouts; the next best corrects it at the first sign.

sentences.zh: 況乎事情已露，禍難垂成，委而不謀，何以寧亂！

translations.literal: How much more when the facts are already exposed and disaster hangs on the verge—to leave it unplanned, how can disorder be stilled!
translations.idiomatic: When the signs are already plain and disaster is at hand, how can we leave it unplanned and still hope to still the realm!

sentences.zh: 李晟見機慮變，先請移軍就東，建徽、惠元勢轉孤弱，為其吞噬，理在必然，它日雖有良圖，亦恐不能自拔。

translations.literal: Li Sheng saw the moment and feared change, asking first to move his army east; Jianhui and Huiyuan grow ever more isolated and weak and will be swallowed by him—this is logically inevitable; even if they have good plans another day, I fear they will not be able to extricate themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng saw the danger and moved east first; Jianhui and Huiyuan grow ever more isolated and will surely be swallowed—later plans may come too late to save them.

sentences.zh: 拯其危急，唯在此時。

translations.literal: To rescue them in their crisis—only at this moment.
translations.idiomatic: To save them, the moment is now.

sentences.zh: 今因李晟願行，便遣合軍同往，託言晟兵素少，慮為賊泚所邀，借此兩軍迭為掎角，仍先諭旨，密使促裝，詔書至營，即日進路，懷光意雖不欲，然亦計無所施。

translations.literal: Now, since Li Sheng is willing to go, send the united armies together, alleging that Sheng's troops have always been few and fearing interception by the rebel Ci, use these two armies in mutual support, first announce the intent in secret and urge them to pack, and when the edict reaches camp let them march that very day; though Huaiguang may be unwilling in heart, he will have no stratagem to apply.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Sheng is willing to move, order the other two armies to march with him, alleging that his force is small and might be cut off by Ci's rebels, so that the three may support one another; announce the intent in secret, urge them to pack, and when the edict reaches camp let them march that day—Huaiguang may dislike it, but he will have no recourse.

sentences.zh: 是謂稱人有奪人之心，疾雷不及掩耳者也。」

translations.literal: This is what is meant by seizing another's intent before he can seize yours—thunder too swift for the ears to cover."
translations.idiomatic: This is what it means to strike before the other can strike—thunder too swift to cover the ears against."

sentences.zh: 解斗不可以不離，救焚不可以不疾，理盡於此，惟陛下圖之。

translations.literal: To break up a fight one must separate the combatants; to save from fire one must act swiftly—the reasoning is complete in this; may Your Majesty consider it."
translations.idiomatic: To end a fight you must separate the fighters; to fight a fire you must act fast—the logic is complete here; I beg Your Majesty to act on it.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿所料極善。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Your forecast is excellent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Your reasoning is excellent.

sentences.zh: 然李晟移軍，懷光不免悵望，若更遣建徽、惠元就東，恐因此生辭，轉難調息，且更俟旬時。」

translations.literal: Yet with Li Sheng's transfer, Huaiguang must feel aggrieved; if we further send Jianhui and Huiyuan east, I fear he will seize on this as a pretext and reconciliation will grow harder—let us wait another ten days."
translations.idiomatic: Yet Li Sheng's move will surely leave Huaiguang resentful; if we send Jianhui and Huiyuan east as well, he may seize on it as a grievance and make matters harder to settle—let us wait another ten days."

sentences.zh: 辛酉，加王武俊同平章事兼幽州、盧龍節度使。

translations.literal: On the day xinyou, Wang Wujun was promoted to Associate Grand Councillor and concurrently military commissioner of Youzhou and Lulong.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinyou day, Wang Wujun was made Associate Grand Councillor and concurrent military commissioner of Youzhou and Lulong.

sentences.zh: 李晟以為：「懷光反狀已明，緩急宜有備，蜀、漢之路不可壅，請以裨將趙光銑等為洋、利、劍三州刺史，各將兵五百以防未然。」

translations.literal: Li Sheng held that "Huaiguang's rebellious signs are already clear; in emergency we should be prepared; the routes to Shu and Han must not be blocked—I ask that the subordinate generals Zhao Guangxian and others be made prefects of Yang, Li, and Jian, each leading five hundred troops to guard against what has not yet happened."
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng argued, "Huaiguang's treason is already plain; we should prepare for the worst. The roads to Shu and Han must not be blocked—I ask that subordinates such as Zhao Guangxian be made prefects of Yang, Li, and Jian, each with five hundred men to guard against what may come."

sentences.zh: 上疑未決，欲親總禁兵幸咸陽，以慰撫為名，趣諸將進討。

translations.literal: The emperor hesitated and had not decided; he wished personally to lead the palace armies to Xianyang, under the name of consolation, to urge the generals forward in the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hesitated; he considered leading the palace armies personally to Xianyang on a mission of reassurance, to hurry the generals into action.

sentences.zh: 或謂懷光曰：「此漢祖游雲夢之策也！」

translations.literal: Someone said to Huaiguang, "This is the stratagem by which the Han Founder toured Yunmeng!"
translations.idiomatic: Someone told Huaiguang, "This is the stratagem of the Han Founder's tour of Yunmeng!"

sentences.zh: 懷光大懼，反謀益甚。

translations.literal: Huaiguang was greatly afraid and his rebellious designs grew stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang was terrified, and his plans for rebellion grew bolder.

sentences.zh: 上垂欲行，懷光辭益不遜，上猶疑讒人間之，甲子，加懷光太尉，增實食，賜鐵券，遣神策右兵馬使李卞等往諭旨。

translations.literal: The emperor was on the verge of going; Huaiguang's words grew ever more disrespectful. The emperor still suspected that slanderers were setting them at odds. On the day jiazi he promoted Huaiguang to Grand Mentor, increased his substantive income, bestowed an iron certificate, and sent Li Bian of the Shence Right Army and others to announce the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor was about to set out, Huaiguang's language grew ever more insolent; the emperor still suspected men of driving them apart. On the jiazi day he promoted Huaiguang to Grand Mentor, increased his income, granted an iron certificate, and sent Li Bian of the Shence Right Army and others to announce the imperial will.

sentences.zh: 懷光對使者投鐵券於地曰：「聖人疑懷光邪？

translations.literal: Huaiguang faced the envoys, cast the iron certificate to the ground, and said, "Does the Sage suspect Huaiguang?
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang faced the envoys, threw the iron certificate to the ground, and said, "Does His Majesty suspect me?

sentences.zh: 人臣反，賜鐵券；

translations.literal: When a minister rebels, an iron certificate is granted;
translations.idiomatic: When a minister rebels, he is given an iron certificate;

sentences.zh: 懷光不反，今賜鐵券，是使之反也！」

translations.literal: Huaiguang has not rebelled—now to grant an iron certificate is to make him rebel!"
translations.idiomatic: I have not rebelled—yet now you grant me one. You are forcing me to rebel!"

sentences.zh: 辭氣甚悖。

translations.literal: His tone was very defiant.
translations.idiomatic: His tone was openly defiant.

sentences.zh: 朔方左兵馬使張名振當軍門大呼曰：「太尉視賊不許擊，待天使不敬，果欲反邪！

translations.literal: Zhang Mingzhen, left army horse commissioner of Shuofang, shouted before the camp gate, "The Grand Mentor sees the rebels and will not permit an attack, treats the imperial envoy without respect—do you truly intend to rebel!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mingzhen, left army horse commissioner of Shuofang, shouted at the camp gate, "Grand Mentor, you will not let us strike the rebels and you treat the imperial envoy with contempt—do you mean to rebel after all!

sentences.zh: 功高太山，一旦棄之，自取族滅，富貴他人，何益哉！

translations.literal: Your merit towers like Mount Tai, yet you cast it aside in a day, bringing extinction on your clan and enriching others—of what use is that!
translations.idiomatic: Your merit towers like Mount Tai, yet you throw it away in a day, destroy your own house, and enrich others—what good is that to you!

sentences.zh: 我今日必以死爭之！」

translations.literal: Today I will dispute this unto death!"
translations.idiomatic: Today I will dispute this with my life!"

sentences.zh: 懷光聞之，謂曰：「我不反，以賊方強，故須蓄銳俟時耳。」

translations.literal: Hearing this, Huaiguang said, "I am not rebelling; the rebels are still strong, so we must store our edge and await the moment."
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang heard him and said, "I am not rebelling; the rebels are still strong, and we must husband our strength until the time is right."

sentences.zh: 懷光又言：「天子所居必有城隍。」

translations.literal: Huaiguang also said, "Where the Son of Heaven dwells there must be walls and moats."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Where the Son of Heaven dwells there must be fortifications."

sentences.zh: 乃發卒城咸陽，未幾，移軍據之。

translations.literal: He thereupon sent troops to wall Xianyang; before long he moved his army to occupy it.
translations.idiomatic: He sent troops to fortify Xianyang and soon moved his army to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 張名振曰：「乃者言不反，今日拔軍此來，何也？

translations.literal: Zhang Mingzhen said, "Just now you said you would not rebel—today you march your army here; why?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mingzhen said, "You said you would not rebel—yet today you march your army here. Why?

sentences.zh: 何不攻長安，殺朱泚，取富貴，引軍還邠邪？」

translations.literal: Why not attack Chang'an, kill Zhu Ci, win wealth and rank, and lead the army back to Bin?"
translations.idiomatic: Why not attack Chang'an, kill Zhu Ci, win wealth and rank, and march the army back to Bin?"

sentences.zh: 懷光曰：「名振病心矣！」

translations.literal: Huaiguang said, "Mingzhen is sick at heart!"
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang said, "Mingzhen has lost his mind!"

sentences.zh: 命左右引去，拉殺之。

translations.literal: He ordered his attendants to lead him away and had him strangled to death.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his attendants to take him away and had him strangled.

sentences.zh: 右武鋒兵馬使石演芬，本西域胡人，懷光養以為子。

translations.literal: Shi Yanfen, army horse commissioner of the Right Martial Vanguard, was originally a barbarian of the Western Regions whom Huaiguang had raised as a son.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yanfen, army horse commissioner of the Right Martial Vanguard, was originally a man of the Western Regions whom Huaiguang had adopted as a son.

sentences.zh: 懷光潛與朱泚通謀，演芬遣其客郜成義詣行在告之，請罷其都統之權。

translations.literal: Huaiguang secretly communicated with Zhu Ci in conspiracy; Yanfen sent his client Gao Chengyi to the traveling court to report this and ask that Huaiguang's supreme command be removed.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang was secretly in league with Zhu Ci; Yanfen sent his client Gao Chengyi to the traveling court to expose the plot and ask that Huaiguang be stripped of supreme command.

sentences.zh: 成義至奉天，告懷光子璀。

translations.literal: Chengyi reached Fengtian and told Huaiguang's son Cui.
translations.idiomatic: Chengyi reached Fengtian and told Huaiguang's son Cui.

sentences.zh: 璀密白其父。

translations.literal: Cui secretly informed his father.
translations.idiomatic: Cui secretly informed his father.

sentences.zh: 懷光召演芬責之曰：「我以爾為子，奈何欲破我家！

translations.literal: Huaiguang summoned Yanfen and rebuked him, saying, "I took you as a son—how dare you seek to destroy my house!
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang summoned Yanfen and rebuked him: "I took you as my son—how dare you seek to destroy my house!

sentences.zh: 今日負我，死甘心乎？」

translations.literal: Today you betray me—are you content to die?"
translations.idiomatic: Today you betray me—are you willing to die for it?"

sentences.zh: 演芬曰：「天子以太尉為股肱，太尉以演芬為心腹；

translations.literal: Yanfen said, "The Son of Heaven takes the Grand Mentor as his right arm; the Grand Mentor takes Yanfen as his heart;
translations.idiomatic: Yanfen said, "The Son of Heaven made you his right arm, and you made me your trusted man;

sentences.zh: 太尉既負天子，演芬安得不負太尉乎！

translations.literal: the Grand Mentor has already betrayed the Son of Heaven—how can Yanfen not betray the Grand Mentor!
translations.idiomatic: you have betrayed the Son of Heaven—how can I not betray you!

sentences.zh: 演芬胡人，不能異心，惟知事一人。

translations.literal: Yanfen is a barbarian and cannot harbor two loyalties; he knows only to serve one man.
translations.idiomatic: I am a barbarian and cannot serve two masters; I know only to serve one man.

sentences.zh: 苟免賊名而死，死甘心矣！」

translations.literal: If I may die free of the name of traitor, I die content!"
translations.idiomatic: If I may die without the name of traitor, I die content!"

sentences.zh: 懷光使左右臠食之，皆曰：「義士也，可令快死！」

translations.literal: Huaiguang had his attendants cut him to pieces; all said, "A man of righteousness—let him die swiftly!"
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang ordered his men to cut him to pieces; they all said, "A righteous man—let him die quickly!"

sentences.zh: 以刀斷其喉而去。

translations.literal: They cut his throat with a blade and left him.
translations.idiomatic: They cut his throat and left him.

sentences.zh: 李卞等還，言懷光驕慢之狀，於是行在始嚴門禁，從臣皆密裝以待。

translations.literal: When Li Bian and the others returned and reported Huaiguang's arrogant disrespect, the traveling court then tightened gate security, and the attending officials all secretly packed in readiness.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bian and the others returned and reported Huaiguang's arrogance; the traveling court then tightened security, and the officials all packed in secret against what might come.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，加李晟河中、同絳節度使。

translations.literal: On the day yichou, Li Sheng was promoted to military commissioner of Hezhong, Tong, and Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: On the yichou day, Li Sheng was made military commissioner of Hezhong, Tong, and Jiang.

sentences.zh: 上猶以為薄，丙寅，又加同平章事。

translations.literal: The emperor still thought this meager; on the day bingyin he was further made Associate Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still thought this insufficient; on the bingyin day he was also made Associate Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 上將幸梁州，山南節度使鹽亭嚴震聞之，遣使詣奉天奉迎，又遣大將張用誠將兵五千至盩厔以來迎衛。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to visit Liangzhou; Yan Zhen, military commissioner of Shannan at Yanting, heard of this and sent envoys to Fengtian to welcome him, and also sent the great general Zhang Yongcheng with five thousand troops to Zhouzhi to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor prepared to go to Liangzhou, Yan Zhen, military commissioner of Shannan, sent envoys to Fengtian to welcome him and dispatched Zhang Yongcheng with five thousand men to Zhouzhi as escort.

sentences.zh: 用誠為懷光所誘，陰與之通謀，上聞而患之。

translations.literal: Yongcheng was enticed by Huaiguang and secretly communicated with him in conspiracy; when the emperor heard of this he was troubled.
translations.idiomatic: Yongcheng had been won over by Huaiguang and was secretly in league with him; when the emperor learned of this he was alarmed.

sentences.zh: 會震繼遣牙將馬勳奉表，上語之故。

translations.literal: It happened that Zhen next sent his adjutant general Ma Xun to present a memorial; the emperor told him the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen then sent his adjutant Ma Xun with a memorial, and the emperor explained what had happened.

sentences.zh: 勳請：「亟詣梁州取嚴震符召用誠還府，若不受召，臣請殺之。」

translations.literal: Xun requested, "Let me hurry to Liangzhou to obtain Yan Zhen's tally and summon Yongcheng back to headquarters; if he does not obey the summons, I ask to kill him."
translations.idiomatic: Xun asked, "Let me go at once to Liangzhou for Commissioner Yan's tally to recall Yongcheng; if he refuses, I will kill him."

sentences.zh: 上喜曰：「卿何時復至此？」

translations.literal: The emperor said with pleasure, "When did you return to us?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said gladly, "When did you come back to us?"

sentences.zh: 勳刻日時而去。

translations.literal: Xun set a day and hour and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Xun fixed a day and hour and set out.

sentences.zh: 既得震符，請壯士五人與之俱出駱谷。

translations.literal: Once he had obtained Zhen's tally, he asked for five stalwart men to go with him out through Luogu Valley.
translations.idiomatic: With Yan's tally in hand, he took five strong men and went out through Luogu Valley.

sentences.zh: 用誠不知事洩，以數百騎迎之，勳與之俱入驛。

translations.literal: Yongcheng did not know the affair had leaked; he came to meet him with several hundred horsemen, and Xun entered the post station with him.
translations.idiomatic: Yongcheng did not know the plot was exposed; he met Xun with several hundred horsemen, and Xun entered the post station with him.

sentences.zh: 時天寒，勳多然蒿火於驛外，軍士皆往附火。

translations.literal: The weather was cold; Xun lit many fires of wormwood outside the station, and the soldiers all went to warm themselves at the flames.
translations.idiomatic: It was bitter cold; Xun lit many fires of wormwood outside the station, and the soldiers all went to warm themselves.

sentences.zh: 勳乃從容出懷中符，以示用誠曰：「大夫召君。」

translations.literal: Xun then calmly drew the tally from his breast and showed it to Yongcheng, saying, "The Commissioner summons you."
translations.idiomatic: Xun then calmly produced the tally from his breast and showed Yongcheng: "The Commissioner summons you."

sentences.zh: 用誠錯愕起走，壯士自後執其手擒之。

translations.literal: Yongcheng started up in alarm to flee; the stalwarts seized his hands from behind and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Yongcheng started up in alarm to flee; the stalwarts seized him from behind.

sentences.zh: 用誠子在勳後，斫傷勳首。

translations.literal: Yongcheng's son was behind Xun and hacked at Xun's head, wounding him.
translations.idiomatic: Yongcheng's son was behind Xun and hacked at his head, wounding him.

sentences.zh: 壯士格殺其子，僕用誠於地，跨其腹，以刀擬其喉曰：「出聲則死！」

translations.literal: The stalwarts killed his son in the struggle, threw Yongcheng to the ground, straddled his belly, and held a blade to his throat, saying, "Make a sound and you die!"
translations.idiomatic: The stalwarts killed his son, threw Yongcheng down, straddled him, and held a blade to his throat: "Make a sound and you die!"

sentences.zh: 勳入其營，士卒已擐甲執兵矣。

translations.literal: Xun entered the camp; the soldiers had already donned armor and taken up weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Xun entered the camp; the soldiers had already armed themselves.

sentences.zh: 勳大言曰：「汝曹父母妻子皆在漢中，一朝棄之，與張用誠同反，於汝曹何利乎！

translations.literal: Xun cried aloud, "Your fathers and mothers, wives and children are all in Hanzhong—you would abandon them in a day and rebel with Zhang Yongcheng; what profit is there in that for you!
translations.idiomatic: Xun shouted, "Your parents, wives, and children are all in Hanzhong—you would abandon them in a day and rebel with Zhang Yongcheng; what good is that to you!

sentences.zh: 大夫令我取用誠，不問汝曹，無自取族滅！」

translations.literal: The Commissioner ordered me to take Yongcheng and does not question you—do not bring extinction on your clans yourselves!"
translations.idiomatic: The Commissioner sent me for Yongcheng alone—do not bring ruin on your own houses!"

sentences.zh: 眾皆讋服。

translations.literal: The crowd all submitted in fear.
translations.idiomatic: The men all submitted in fear.

sentences.zh: 勳送用誠詣梁州，震杖殺之，命副將領其眾。

translations.literal: Xun sent Yongcheng to Liangzhou; Zhen had him beaten to death with the staff and ordered a deputy general to take command of his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Xun sent Yongcheng to Liangzhou; Yan had him beaten to death and put a deputy in command of his troops.

sentences.zh: 勳裹其首，覆命於行在，愆期半日。

translations.literal: Xun wrapped up his head and reported back to the traveling court, half a day past the appointed time.
translations.idiomatic: Xun wrapped up Yongcheng's head and reported to the traveling court, only half a day late.

sentences.zh: 李懷光夜遣人襲奪李建徽、楊惠元軍，建徽走免，惠元將奔奉天，懷光遣兵追殺之。

translations.literal: By night Li Huaiguang sent men to raid and seize the armies of Li Jianhui and Yang Huiyuan; Jianhui fled and escaped, while Huiyuan was about to flee to Fengtian when Huaiguang sent troops in pursuit and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huaiguang sent men by night to overrun the armies of Li Jianhui and Yang Huiyuan; Jianhui escaped, but Huiyuan, fleeing toward Fengtian, was overtaken and killed.

sentences.zh: 懷光又宣言曰：「吾今與朱泚連和，車駕且光遠避！」

translations.literal: Huaiguang also proclaimed, "I am now allied with Zhu Ci; let the imperial carriage make haste to keep its distance!"
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang also proclaimed, "I am now allied with Zhu Ci; let the imperial carriage withdraw far and fast!"

sentences.zh: 懷光以韓游瑰朔方將也，掌兵在奉天，與游瑰書，約使為變，游瑰密奏之。

translations.literal: Huaiguang, because Han Yougui was a Shuofang general holding troops at Fengtian, wrote to Yougui inviting him to join in revolt; Yougui secretly memorialized this.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang knew Han Yougui was a Shuofang general with troops at Fengtian and wrote inviting him to rebel; Yougui secretly reported it.

sentences.zh: 明日，又以書趣之，游瑰又奏之。

translations.literal: The next day he again wrote to urge him; Yougui memorialized again.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he wrote again to urge him on; Yougui reported again.

sentences.zh: 上稱其忠義，因問：「策安出？」

translations.literal: The emperor praised his loyalty and righteousness and asked, "What strategy do you propose?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his loyalty and asked, "What is your plan?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「懷光總諸道兵，故敢恃眾為亂。

translations.literal: He replied, "Huaiguang commands the armies of all circuits and therefore dares rely on his numbers to make disorder.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Huaiguang commands the armies of all circuits and therefore dares rebel on the strength of his numbers.

sentences.zh: 今邠寧有張昕，靈武有寧景璿，河中有呂鳴岳，振武有杜從政，潼關有唐朝臣，渭北有竇覦，皆守將也。

translations.literal: Now at Bin-Ning there is Zhang Xin, at Lingwu Ning Jingxuan, at Hezhong Lü Mingyue, at Zhenwu Du Congzheng, at Tong Pass Tang Chaochen, and on the north bank of the Wei Dou Kan—all garrison commanders.
translations.idiomatic: At Bin-Ning there is Zhang Xin; at Lingwu, Ning Jingxuan; at Hezhong, Lü Mingyue; at Zhenwu, Du Congzheng; at Tong Pass, Tang Chaochen; on the north bank of the Wei, Dou Kan—all garrison commanders.

sentences.zh: 陛下各以其眾及地授之，尊懷光之官，罷其權，則行營諸將各受本府指麾矣。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty grants each his troops and territory, honors Huaiguang in rank but removes his authority, then the generals of the field camps will each take orders from their home commands.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty gives each his troops and territory, honors Huaiguang in title but strips his command, the field generals will each answer to their own headquarters.

sentences.zh: 懷光獨立，安能為亂！」

translations.literal: Huaiguang standing alone—how can he make disorder!"
translations.idiomatic: Left alone, how can Huaiguang rebel!"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「罷懷光兵權，若朱泚何？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "If we remove Huaiguang's military authority, what of Zhu Ci?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "If we strip Huaiguang of command, what of Zhu Ci?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下既許將士以克城殊賞，將士奉天子之命以討賊取富貴，誰不願之！

translations.literal: He replied, "Your Majesty has already promised the officers and men exceptional rewards for taking the city; the officers and men, obeying the Son of Heaven's command to punish rebels and win wealth and rank—who would not wish it!
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Your Majesty has promised extraordinary rewards for taking the city; who among the troops would not gladly obey the Son of Heaven, strike the rebels, and win wealth and rank!

sentences.zh: 邠府兵以萬數，借使臣得而將之，足以誅泚。

translations.literal: The Bin prefecture troops number in the tens of thousands; grant me command of them and they are enough to execute Ci.
translations.idiomatic: The Bin troops number in the tens of thousands; give me command of them and they are enough to destroy Ci.

sentences.zh: 況諸道必有杖義之臣，泚不足憂也！」

translations.literal: Moreover, among the circuits there will surely be ministers who uphold righteousness—Ci is not worth worrying over!"
translations.idiomatic: And among the circuits there will surely be men who take the righteous side—Ci is nothing to fear!"

sentences.zh: 上然之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，懷光遣其將趙升鸞入奉天，約其夕使別將達奚小俊燒乾陵，令升鸞為內應以驚脅乘輿。

translations.literal: On the day dingmao, Huaiguang sent his general Zhao Shengluan into Fengtian, arranging that night for another general, Dada Xiaojun, to burn Qianling and ordering Shengluan to act as inside collaborator to frighten and coerce the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingmao day, Huaiguang sent his general Zhao Shengluan into Fengtian, planning that night for Dada Xiaojun to burn Qianling while Shengluan acted within as accomplice to terrify the emperor into flight.

sentences.zh: 升鸞詣渾瑊自言，瑊遽以聞，且請決幸梁州。

translations.literal: Shengluan went to Hun Jian and confessed; Jian hurriedly reported it and asked that the decision be made to visit Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shengluan went to Hun Jian and confessed; Jian reported at once and urged the emperor to flee to Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 上命瑊戒嚴，瑊出，部勒未畢，上已出城西，命戴休顏守奉天，朝臣將士狼狽扈從。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Jian to impose martial law; Jian went out, and before the muster was finished the emperor had already left by the west gate, ordering Dai Xiuyan to hold Fengtian while courtiers and officers followed in disarray.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Jian to impose martial law; before Jian had finished mustering the troops, the emperor was already out the west gate, leaving Dai Xiuyan to hold Fengtian while courtiers and soldiers followed in disorder.

sentences.zh: 戴休顏徇於軍中曰：「懷光已反！」

translations.literal: Dai Xiuyan proclaimed through the army, "Huaiguang has rebelled!"
translations.idiomatic: Dai Xiuyan proclaimed through the ranks, "Huaiguang has rebelled!"

sentences.zh: 遂乘城拒守。

translations.literal: and thereupon mounted the walls to resist and defend.
translations.idiomatic: And at once he manned the walls to defend the city.

sentences.zh: 朱泚之稱帝也，兵部侍郎劉乃臥病在家，泚召之，不起。

translations.literal: When Zhu Ci declared himself emperor, Liu Nai, vice minister of war, lay ill at home; Ci summoned him, but he would not rise.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci declared himself emperor, Liu Nai, Vice Minister of War, lay ill at home; Ci summoned him, but he would not come.

sentences.zh: 使蔣鎮自往說之，凡再往，知不可誘脅，乃歎曰：「鎮亦忝列曹，不能捨生，以至於此，豈可復以己之腥臊污漫賢者乎！」

translations.literal: Ci sent Jiang Zhen in person to persuade him; Zhen went twice in all, saw that he could not be enticed or coerced, and sighed, "I too hold office in this ministry and cannot give up my life, yet have come to this—how can I again defile a worthy man with my own foulness!"
translations.idiomatic: Ci sent Jiang Zhen to persuade him; Zhen went twice and saw he could not be moved, then sighed, "I too hold office in this ministry and could not give up my life, yet have come to this—how can I defile a worthy man with my own foulness!"

sentences.zh: 歔郗而返。

translations.literal: He sobbed and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He sobbed and went back.

sentences.zh: 乃聞帝幸山南，搏膺大呼，自投於床，不食，數日而卒。

translations.literal: When Liu Nai heard the emperor had gone to Shannan, he beat his breast and cried aloud, threw himself on his bed, ate nothing, and died within several days.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Nai heard the emperor had fled to Shannan, he beat his breast and cried out, threw himself on his bed, refused food, and died within days.

sentences.zh: 太子少師喬琳從上至盩厔，稱老疾不堪山險，削髮為僧，匿於仙遊寺。

translations.literal: Qiao Lin, junior preceptor to the heir apparent, followed the emperor to Zhouzhi, pleaded old age and illness unfit for mountain perils, shaved his head to become a monk, and hid in Xianyou Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Lin, Junior Preceptor to the Heir Apparent, followed the emperor to Zhouzhi, pleaded age and illness unfit for mountain roads, shaved his head as a monk, and hid in Xianyou Temple.

sentences.zh: 泚聞之，召至長安，以為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Ci heard of this, summoned him to Chang'an, and made him Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Ci heard of it, summoned him to Chang'an, and made him Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 於是朝士之竄匿者多出仕泚矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon many court officials who had fled and hidden themselves came out to serve Ci.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter many court officials who had been in hiding came out to serve Ci.

sentences.zh: 懷光遣其將孟保、惠靜壽、孫福達將精騎趣南山邀車駕，遇諸軍糧料使張增於盩厔。

translations.literal: Huaiguang sent his generals Meng Bao, Hui Jingshou, and Sun Fuda with picked cavalry toward the Southern Mountains to intercept the imperial carriage; they met Zhang Zeng, commissary for provisions of the various armies, at Zhouzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang sent his generals Meng Bao, Hui Jingshou, and Sun Fuda with elite cavalry toward the Southern Mountains to intercept the emperor; at Zhouzhi they met Zhang Zeng, commissary for the armies' provisions.

sentences.zh: 三將曰：「彼使我為不臣，我以追不及報之，不過不使我將耳。」

translations.literal: The three generals said, "He would have us be disloyal subjects; we shall report that we could not overtake them—at worst he will merely not let us command troops."
translations.idiomatic: The three generals said, "He would make us traitors; we shall report we could not overtake the emperor—at worst he will only strip us of command."

sentences.zh: 因目增曰：「軍士未朝食，如何？」

translations.literal: They then signaled Zeng and said, "The soldiers have not eaten this morning—what shall we do?"
translations.idiomatic: They signaled to Zeng: "The men have not eaten this morning—what shall we do?"

sentences.zh: 增紿其眾曰：「此東數里有佛祠，吾貯糧焉。」

translations.literal: Zeng deceived the crowd, saying, "Several li east of here is a Buddhist shrine where I have stored grain."
translations.idiomatic: Zeng deceived them: "A few li east is a Buddhist shrine where I have stored grain."

sentences.zh: 三將帥眾而東，縱之剽掠，由是百官從行者皆得入駱谷，以追不及還報，懷光皆黜之。

translations.literal: The three generals led the troops east and let them plunder; thereby all the officials traveling with the emperor were able to enter Luogu Valley. Reporting that they could not overtake the party, they were all dismissed by Huaiguang.
translations.idiomatic: The three generals led their men east and let them loot; meanwhile the officials with the emperor escaped into Luogu Valley. Reporting failure to overtake them, all three were dismissed by Huaiguang.

sentences.zh: 河東將王權、馬匯引兵歸太原。

translations.literal: The Hedong generals Wang Quan and Ma Hui led their troops back to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Hedong generals Wang Quan and Ma Hui marched their troops back to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 李晟得除官制，拜哭受命，謂將佐曰：「長安，宗廟所在，天下根本，若諸將皆從行，誰當滅賊者！」

translations.literal: Li Sheng received the appointment edict, bowed and wept as he accepted the commission, and said to his officers, "Chang'an is where the ancestral temples stand and the root of the realm—if all the generals follow the emperor on the road, who will destroy the rebels!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng received his appointment, bowed and wept as he accepted it, and told his officers, "Chang'an holds the ancestral temples and is the root of the realm—if every general follows the emperor south, who will destroy the rebels!"

sentences.zh: 乃治城隍，繕甲兵，為復京城之計。

translations.literal: He thereupon repaired walls and moats, readied armor and weapons, and planned for the recovery of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He fortified his position, readied arms and armor, and set about recovering the capital.

sentences.zh: 先是東渭橋有積粟十餘萬斛，度支給李懷光軍，凡盡。

translations.literal: Earlier there had been more than one hundred thousand bushels of grain stored at East Wei Bridge; the Department of Revenue supplied Li Huaiguang's army until it was all gone.
translations.idiomatic: East Wei Bridge had held more than one hundred thousand bushels of grain; the revenue office had issued it all to Li Huaiguang's army.

sentences.zh: 是時懷光、朱泚連兵，聲勢甚盛，車駕南幸，人情擾擾。

translations.literal: At this time Huaiguang and Zhu Ci had joined forces; their momentum was very strong, the imperial carriage had gone south, and popular sentiment was in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang and Zhu Ci had joined forces; their power was formidable, the emperor had fled south, and the realm was in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 晟以孤軍處二強寇之間，內無資糧，外無救援，徒以忠義感激將士，故其眾雖單弱而銳氣不衰。

translations.literal: Sheng, with a lone army between two powerful foes, had no supplies within and no relief from without; he relied only on loyalty and righteousness to move his officers and men, and therefore though his force was few and weak its keen spirit did not fade.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng stood alone between two powerful enemies, without supplies within or aid without; he moved his men only by loyalty and righteousness, and though his force was small its fighting spirit never waned.

sentences.zh: 又以書遣懷光，辭禮卑遜，雖示尊崇而諭以禍福，勸之立功補過。

translations.literal: He also sent a letter to Huaiguang with humble and deferential wording; though showing respect, he explained fortune and misfortune and urged him to achieve merit and redeem his faults.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote to Huaiguang in humble, deferential terms, showing respect while explaining the consequences and urging him to redeem himself through merit.

sentences.zh: 故懷光慚恧，未忍擊之。

translations.literal: Therefore Huaiguang felt shame and could not bring himself to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang was shamed and could not bring himself to attack him.

sentences.zh: 晟曰：「畿內雖兵荒之餘，猶可賦斂。

translations.literal: Sheng said, "Though the capital region has suffered the aftermath of war and famine, levies can still be collected.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said, "Though the capital region has been ravaged by war, taxes can still be collected.

sentences.zh: 宿兵養寇，患莫大焉！」

translations.literal: To quarter troops and nourish the enemy—no calamity is greater!"
translations.idiomatic: To keep troops idle while the enemy grows strong is the greatest danger!"

sentences.zh: 乃以判官張彧假京兆尹，擇四十餘人，假官以督渭北諸縣芻粟，不旬日，皆充羨。

translations.literal: He thereupon had his aide Zhang Yu act as provisional metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, chose more than forty men, and gave them provisional offices to oversee fodder and grain in the counties north of the Wei; within ten days all stores were full.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed his aide Zhang Yu acting metropolitan governor, chose more than forty men as provisional officials to gather fodder and grain from the counties north of the Wei, and within ten days the stores were full.

sentences.zh: 乃流涕誓眾，決志平賊。

translations.literal: He then wept as he swore before the army and resolved to pacify the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: He wept as he swore before his army and resolved to crush the rebels.

sentences.zh: 田悅用兵數敗，士卒死者什六七，其下皆厭苦之。

translations.literal: Tian Yue had been defeated repeatedly in battle; six or seven tenths of his soldiers had died, and his subordinates were all weary and bitter.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue had lost battle after battle; six or seven tenths of his soldiers were dead, and his men were weary and bitter.

sentences.zh: 上以給事中孔巢父為魏博宣慰使。

translations.literal: The emperor appointed Kong Chaofu, supervising secretary, as pacification commissioner to Weibo.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Kong Chaofu, Supervising Secretary, as pacification commissioner to Weibo.

sentences.zh: 巢父性辯博，至魏州，對其眾為陳逆順禍福，悅及將士皆喜。

translations.literal: Chaofu was eloquent and learned; arriving at Weizhou, he addressed the assembly on the fortune and misfortune of loyalty and rebellion, and Yue and the officers and men were all pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Chaofu was eloquent and learned; at Weizhou he addressed the troops on the rewards of loyalty and the cost of rebellion, and Yue and his men were pleased.

sentences.zh: 兵馬使田緒，承嗣之子也，凶險，多過失，悅不忍殺，杖而拘之。

translations.literal: Tian Xu, army horse commissioner, was Chengsi's son—fierce and dangerous, with many faults; Yue could not bear to kill him and had him beaten and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Xu, army horse commissioner and son of Tian Chengsi, was violent and erratic; Yue could not bring himself to execute him and had him beaten and imprisoned instead.

sentences.zh: 悅既歸國，內外撤警備。

translations.literal: Once Yue had returned to allegiance, inner and outer guards were relaxed.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yue had submitted again to the throne, security was relaxed inside and out.

sentences.zh: 三月，壬申朔，悅與孔巢父宴飲，緒對弟侄有怨言，其侄止之，緒怒，殺侄，既而悔之，曰：「僕射必殺我！」

translations.literal: In the third month, on the first day renshen, Yue feasted and drank with Kong Chaofu; Xu complained against his younger brothers and nephews, a nephew tried to stop him, Xu in anger killed the nephew, then repented and said, "The Commissioner will surely kill me!"
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the first day of the cycle, Yue feasted with Kong Chaofu; Xu complained bitterly about his younger kin, a nephew tried to restrain him, and Xu in anger killed the nephew, then said in remorse, "The Commissioner will surely kill me!"

sentences.zh: 既夕，悅醉，歸寢，緒與左右密穿後坦入，殺悅及其母、妻等十餘人，即帥左右執刀立於中門之內夾道。

translations.literal: That evening Yue was drunk and went to sleep; Xu and his attendants secretly broke through the rear wall, entered, and killed Yue together with his mother, wife, and more than ten others; he then led his attendants with blades drawn to stand in the inner passage of the central gate.
translations.idiomatic: That evening, when Yue was drunk and asleep, Xu and his men broke through the rear wall, killed Yue along with his mother, wife, and more than ten others, and posted armed men in the inner passage of the central gate.

sentences.zh: 將旦，以悅命召行軍司馬扈崿、判官許士則、都虞候蔣濟議事。

translations.literal: As dawn approached, in Yue's name he summoned the field marshal Hu E, aide Xu Shize, and chief registrar Jiang Ji to discuss affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he summoned, in Yue's name, the field marshal Hu E, aide Xu Shize, and chief registrar Jiang Ji to discuss business.

sentences.zh: 府署深邃，外不知有變，士則、濟先至，召入，亂斫殺之。

translations.literal: The headquarters were deep and remote; those outside did not know of the change. Shize and Ji arrived first, were summoned in, and were hacked to death in the confusion.
translations.idiomatic: The headquarters were deep within the compound and those outside knew nothing; Shize and Ji arrived first, were called in, and were hacked to death.

sentences.zh: 緒恐既明事洩，乃出門，遇悅親將劉忠信方排牙，緒疾呼謂眾曰：「劉忠信與扈崿謀反，昨夜刺殺僕射。」

translations.literal: Xu feared that once it was light the affair would leak out; he went out the gate and met Yue's trusted general Liu Zhongxin just forming ranks for inspection. Xu cried urgently to the crowd, "Liu Zhongxin and Hu E plotted rebellion and stabbed the Commissioner to death last night."
translations.idiomatic: Fearing exposure at daylight, Xu went out and met Yue's trusted general Liu Zhongxin forming ranks for inspection; Xu shouted to the men, "Liu Zhongxin and Hu E rebelled and stabbed the Commissioner last night!"

sentences.zh: 眾大驚，喧嘩。

translations.literal: The crowd was greatly alarmed and clamored.
translations.idiomatic: The men were thrown into alarm and uproar.

sentences.zh: 忠信未及自辨，眾分裂殺之。

translations.literal: Zhongxin had no time to defend himself before the crowd fell upon him in pieces and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Before Zhongxin could defend himself, the men fell on him and killed him.

sentences.zh: 扈崿來，及戟門遇亂，招諭將士，將士從之者三分之一。

translations.literal: Hu E came and, reaching the halberd gate, encountered the disorder; he summoned and addressed the officers and men, and one third of the troops followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Hu E came up to the halberd gate, found chaos, and rallied the troops; one third of the men followed him.

sentences.zh: 緒懼，登城而立，大呼謂眾曰：「緒，先相公之子，諸君受先相公恩，若能立緒，兵馬使賞緡錢二千，大將半之，下至士卒，人賞百緡，竭公私之貨，五日取辦。」

translations.literal: Xu was afraid; he climbed the wall and stood atop the city, shouting loudly to the crowd: "Xu is the son of the late Chancellor; you all received the late Chancellor's favor—if you can install Xu, the commander of horse and infantry will be rewarded two thousand strings of cash, great generals half that amount, down to common soldiers one hundred strings each; public and private stores will be drained, to be ready within five days."
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Xu mounted the wall and cried out to the troops: "I am the late Chancellor's son. You owe him your loyalty—if you make me commander, the cavalry commander gets two thousand strings of cash, senior generals half that, and every soldier down to the ranks one hundred strings. I will empty the treasury, public and private, and have it ready in five days."

sentences.zh: 於是將士回首殺扈崿，皆歸緒，軍府乃定。

translations.literal: Thereupon the officers and men turned back and killed Hu E; all submitted to Xu, and the military headquarters was thereby settled.
translations.idiomatic: The troops wheeled about, killed Hu E, and rallied to Xu; the headquarters was secure.

sentences.zh: 因請命於孔巢父，巢父命緒權知軍府。

translations.literal: He then requested orders from Kong Chaofu; Chaofu ordered Xu to act provisionally as commander of the military headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He sought confirmation from Kong Chaofu, who appointed Xu acting commander of the headquarters.

sentences.zh: 後數日，眾乃知緒殺其兄，雖悔怒，而緒已立，無如之何。

translations.literal: Several days later the masses learned that Xu had killed his elder brother; though regretful and angry, Xu was already established and nothing could be done.
translations.idiomatic: Days later the men learned Xu had murdered his brother. They were furious, but he was already in power and they could do nothing.

sentences.zh: 緒又殺悅親將薛有倫等二十餘人。

translations.literal: Xu also killed more than twenty of Yue's close generals, including Xue Youlun.
translations.idiomatic: Xu then executed more than twenty of Yue's trusted generals, among them Xue Youlun.

sentences.zh: 李抱真、王武俊引兵將救貝州，聞亂，不敢進。

translations.literal: Li Baozhen and Wang Wujun led troops intending to rescue Beizhou; hearing of the turmoil, they did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: Li Baozhen and Wang Wujun were marching to relieve Beizhou, but when they heard of the upheaval they halted and would not go on.

sentences.zh: 朱滔聞悅死，喜曰：「悅負恩，天假手於緒也！」

translations.literal: Zhu Tao heard Yue was dead and said joyfully: "Yue betrayed grace—Heaven has lent its hand through Xu!"
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Tao heard Yue was dead, he exclaimed with delight: "Yue betrayed his obligations—Heaven has struck through Xu!"

sentences.zh: 即遣其執憲大夫鄭景濟等將步騎五千助馬寔，合兵萬二千攻魏州。

translations.literal: He immediately sent his Integrity Enforcement Grandee Zheng Jingji and others with five thousand foot and cavalry to aid Ma Shi; combined forces numbered twelve thousand to attack Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He at once dispatched his Integrity Enforcement Grandee Zheng Jingji and others with five thousand infantry and cavalry to reinforce Ma Shi; their combined force of twelve thousand marched on Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 寔軍王莽河，縱騎兵及回紇四出剽掠。

translations.literal: Shi's army was at Manghe River; he unleashed cavalry and Uyghurs to raid in all directions.
translations.idiomatic: Shi encamped on the Manghe River and sent his cavalry and Uyghur allies out to plunder on every side.

sentences.zh: 滔別遣人入城說緒，許以本道節度使。

translations.literal: Tao separately sent someone into the city to persuade Xu, promising him the military commission of his circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Tao also sent an envoy into the city to win Xu over, offering him the military commission of his own circuit.

sentences.zh: 緒方危迫，遣隨軍侯臧詣貝州送款於滔，滔喜，遣臧還報，使亟定盟約。

translations.literal: Xu was in dire peril; he sent Hou Zang, who accompanied the army, to Beizhou to offer submission to Tao; Tao was pleased and sent Zang back with a report, urging swift conclusion of the alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Hard pressed, Xu sent his aide Hou Zang to Beizhou to submit to Tao. Tao was delighted, sent Zang back, and pressed for a swift alliance.

sentences.zh: 明緒部署城內已定，李抱真、王武俊又遣使詣緒，許以赴援，如悅存日之約。

translations.literal: At dawn Xu had finished deploying within the city; Li Baozhen and Wang Wujun again sent envoys to Xu, promising to come to his rescue as in the agreement when Yue was alive.
translations.idiomatic: By dawn Xu had secured the city. Li Baozhen and Wang Wujun sent envoys again, pledging relief on the same terms they had given Yue in his lifetime.

sentences.zh: 緒召將佐議之，幕僚曾穆、盧南史曰：「用兵雖尚威武，亦本仁義，然後有功。

translations.literal: Xu summoned generals and staff to discuss; staff members Zeng Mu and Lu Nanshi said: "In warfare one may esteem martial might, yet it must be rooted in benevolence and righteousness, and only then can there be achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Xu called his officers and staff to council. The advisers Zeng Mu and Lu Nanshi said: "War may honor force, but it must rest on benevolence and righteousness—only then can it succeed.

sentences.zh: 今幽陵之兵恣行殺掠，白骨蔽野，雖先僕射背德，其民何罪！

translations.literal: Now the Youling army indulges in killing and plunder at will; white bones cover the wilds—though the former Military Commissioner betrayed virtue, what crime have his people committed!
translations.idiomatic: The Youling troops now kill and loot without restraint until the fields are white with bones. The late commissioner may have broken faith, but what have his people done to deserve this!

sentences.zh: 今雖盛強，其亡可跂立而待也。

translations.literal: Though they are strong now, their fall can be awaited standing on tiptoe.
translations.idiomatic: They are mighty for the moment, but their ruin can be watched for on tiptoe.

sentences.zh: 況昭義、恆冀方相與攻之，奈何以目前之急欲從人為返逆乎！

translations.literal: Moreover Zhaoyi and Hengji are jointly attacking them—how can you, for the urgent need of the moment, wish to follow others in turning traitor!
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoyi and Hengji are already striking them together—how can you, for a passing crisis, follow others into open rebellion!

sentences.zh: 不若歸命朝廷，天子方蒙塵於外，聞魏博使至必喜，官爵旋踵而至矣。」

translations.literal: Better to submit to the court; the Son of Heaven is now dust-stained abroad—hearing an envoy from Weibo has come he will surely rejoice, and offices and ranks will arrive in no time."
translations.idiomatic: Better submit to the court. The Son of Heaven is still in exile; when he hears an envoy from Weibo has come he will rejoice, and rank and office will follow at once."

sentences.zh: 緒從之，遣使奉表詣行在，城守以俟命。

translations.literal: Xu agreed; he sent envoys bearing a memorial to the imperial camp and held the city awaiting orders.
translations.idiomatic: Xu took their advice, sent envoys with a memorial to the imperial camp, and held the city awaiting the court's word.

sentences.zh: 上之發奉天也，韓游瑰帥其麾下八百餘人還邠州。

translations.literal: When the Emperor set out from Fengtian, Han Yougui led his subordinates of more than eight hundred back to Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor left Fengtian, Han Yougui took his eight hundred-odd followers back to Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 李懷光以李晟軍浸盛，惡之，欲引軍自咸陽襲東渭橋。

translations.literal: Li Huaiguang, seeing Li Sheng's army growing daily stronger, hated it and wished to lead troops from Xianyang to strike Dongwei Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huaiguang, seeing Li Sheng's army grow stronger day by day, resented him and planned to march from Xianyang and strike Dongwei Bridge.

sentences.zh: 三令其眾，眾不應，竊相謂曰：「若與我曹擊朱泚，惟力是視；

translations.literal: Three times he ordered his troops; they did not respond, whispering among themselves: "If he wants us to strike Zhu Ci, we will exert our strength;
translations.idiomatic: Three times he ordered his men to move; they would not obey, whispering among themselves: "If he sends us against Zhu Ci, we will fight with all our strength;

sentences.zh: 若欲反，我曹有死，不能從也！」

translations.literal: if he wishes to rebel, we would rather die than follow!"
translations.idiomatic: but if he means to rebel, we would rather die than follow him!"

sentences.zh: 懷光知眾不可強，問計於賓佐，節度巡官良鄉李景略曰：「取長安，殺朱泚，散軍還諸道，單騎詣行在，如此，臣節亦未虧，功名猶可保也。」

translations.literal: Huaiguang knew the masses could not be forced; he asked his staff for counsel. Circuit inspector Li Jinglue of Liangxiang said: "Take Chang'an, kill Zhu Ci, disperse the army back to the various circuits, go alone on horseback to the imperial camp—thus your ministerial integrity would not be damaged and fame and merit could still be preserved."
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang saw he could not compel them and asked his advisers for a plan. His circuit inspector Li Jinglue of Liangxiang said: "Take Chang'an, kill Zhu Ci, send the army back to their circuits, and ride alone to the emperor's camp. Your loyalty would stand intact and your reputation could still be saved."

sentences.zh: 頓道懇請，至於流涕，懷光許之。

translations.literal: He pleaded earnestly, even to the point of shedding tears; Huaiguang agreed.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded again and again until tears ran down his face, and Huaiguang agreed.

sentences.zh: 都虞候閻晏等勸懷光東保河中，徐圖去就，懷光乃說其眾曰：「今且屯涇陽，召妻孥於邠，俟至，與之俱往河中。

translations.literal: Chief military adjutant Yan Yan and others urged Huaiguang to move east and hold Hedong, plotting departure at leisure; Huaiguang then told his troops: "For now we shall encamp at Jingyang, summon wives and children from Bin, wait till they arrive, and go together to Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: His chief adjutant Yan Yan and others urged him to move east, secure Hedong, and decide his course later. Huaiguang then told the troops: "We will camp at Jingyang for now, summon our families from Bin, and when they arrive we will all go on to Hedong together.

sentences.zh: 春裝既辦，還攻長安，未晚也。

translations.literal: When spring equipment is ready, we shall return to attack Chang'an—it will not be too late.
translations.idiomatic: When our spring gear is ready we can turn back and take Chang'an—it will not be too late.

sentences.zh: 東方諸縣皆富實，軍發之日，聽爾曹俘掠。」

translations.literal: The eastern counties are all rich; on the day the army sets out, you may loot as you please."
translations.idiomatic: The eastern counties are all wealthy; on the day we march you may plunder as you please."

sentences.zh: 眾許之。

translations.literal: The troops assented.
translations.idiomatic: The men agreed.

sentences.zh: 懷光乃謂景略曰：「曏者之議，軍眾不從，子宜速去，不且見害！」

translations.literal: Huaiguang then said to Jinglue: "The proposal of just now—the army will not follow; you should leave quickly or you will soon be harmed!"
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang then told Jinglue: "The army would not accept what you proposed just now. Leave at once, or you will soon be killed!"

sentences.zh: 遣數騎送之。

translations.literal: He sent several riders to escort him away.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a few horsemen to escort him out.

sentences.zh: 景略出軍門，慟哭曰：「不意此軍一旦陷於不義！」

translations.literal: Jinglue went out the army gate, wailing: "I did not expect this army in one day to sink into unrighteousness!"
translations.idiomatic: Jinglue left the camp gate wailing: "I never thought this army would fall into treachery in a single day!"

sentences.zh: 懷光遣使詣邠州，令留後張昕悉發所留兵萬餘人及行營將士家屬會涇陽，仍遣其將劉禮等將三千餘騎脅遷之。

translations.literal: Huaiguang sent envoys to Binzhou ordering the acting commander Zhang Xin to fully deploy the more than ten thousand troops left there and the families of camp officers and soldiers to assemble at Jingyang; he also sent his general Liu Li and others with more than three thousand horsemen to coerce their relocation.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang sent envoys to Binzhou ordering the acting commander Zhang Xin to march out every one of the ten thousand-odd troops still there, together with the families of the camp officers and men, to join him at Jingyang; he also sent General Liu Li and others with more than three thousand cavalry to force the move.

sentences.zh: 韓游瑰說昕曰：「李太尉功高自棄，已蹈禍機。

translations.literal: Han Yougui persuaded Xin, saying: "Lord Li the Grand Mentor, though his achievements were high, abandoned himself and has already stepped into disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yougui urged Zhang Xin: "Lord Li the Grand Mentor threw away his great achievements and has already walked into ruin.

sentences.zh: 中丞今日可以自求富貴，游瑰請帥麾下以從。」

translations.literal: Today the Vice Commissioner can seek wealth and honor for himself; Yougui asks to lead his subordinates to follow."
translations.idiomatic: Today you, Vice Commissioner, can win wealth and rank for yourself. Yougui asks leave to lead his men and follow you."

sentences.zh: 昕曰：「昕微賤，賴李太尉得至此，不忍負也！」
