translations.literal: Xin said: "Xin is lowly and insignificant; I relied on Lord Li the Grand Mentor to reach this position—I cannot bear to betray him!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xin said: "I am a man of no account. I owe my position to Lord Li the Grand Mentor, and I cannot betray him!"

sentences.zh: 游瑰乃謝病不出，陰與諸將高固、楊懷賓等相結。

translations.literal: Yougui then pleaded illness and did not go out, secretly joining with generals Gao Gu, Yang Huaibin, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Yougui pleaded illness and stayed indoors, secretly joining forces with the generals Gao Gu, Yang Huaibin, and others.

sentences.zh: 時崔漢衡以吐蕃兵營於邠南，高固曰：「昕以眾去，則邠城空矣。」

translations.literal: At that time Cui Hanheng had Tibetan troops camped south of Bin; Gao Gu said: "If Xin goes away with the troops, Bin city will be empty."
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hanheng had Tibetan troops camped south of Bin. Gao Gu said: "If Zhang Xin marches out with the army, Binzhou will be left defenseless."

sentences.zh: 乃詐為渾瑊書，召吐蕃使稍逼邠城。

translations.literal: They forged a letter in the name of Hun Jian, summoning the Tibetans to draw slightly nearer to Bin city.
translations.idiomatic: They forged a letter in Hun Jian's name summoning the Tibetans to press closer to the city.

sentences.zh: 昕等懼，竟不敢出。

translations.literal: Xin and the others were afraid and ultimately did not dare go out.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xin and his party were terrified and in the end did not dare march out.

sentences.zh: 昕等謀殺諸將之不從者，游瑰知之，先與高固等舉兵殺昕，遣楊懷賓奉表以聞，且遣人告崔漢衡。

translations.literal: Xin and the others plotted to kill generals who would not follow; Yougui learned of it and first joined Gao Gu and others in raising troops to kill Xin; he sent Yang Huaibin to present a memorial reporting it and also dispatched someone to inform Cui Hanheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xin planned to kill any general who refused to obey. Yougui learned of it, rose first with Gao Gu and the others, and killed Zhang Xin. He sent Yang Huaibin with a memorial to the throne and a messenger to Cui Hanheng.

sentences.zh: 漢衡矯詔以游瑰知軍府事，軍中大喜。

translations.literal: Hanheng issued a forged edict making Yougui provisional commander of the headquarters; the army was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Hanheng forged an edict appointing Yougui commander of the headquarters, and the army rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 懷光子旻在邠，游瑰遣之，或曰：「不殺旻，何以自明？」

translations.literal: Huaiguang's son Min was at Bin; Yougui released him. Someone said: "If you do not kill Min, how can you prove your loyalty?"
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang's son Min was at Bin. Yougui let him go. Someone said: "If you do not kill Min, how will you prove your loyalty to the court?"

sentences.zh: 游瑰曰：「殺旻，則懷光怒，其眾必至，不如釋旻以走之。」

translations.literal: Yougui said: "If we kill Min, Huaiguang will be enraged and his troops will surely come—it is better to release Min so they flee."
translations.idiomatic: Yougui said: "Kill Min and Huaiguang will rage; his army will come at once. Better release him and let them flee."

sentences.zh: 時楊懷賓子朝晟在懷光軍中為右廂兵馬使，聞之，泣白懷光曰：「父立功於國，子當誅夷，不可典兵。」

translations.literal: At that time Yang Huaibin's son Chaocheng was in Huaiguang's army as commander of the right wing horse and infantry; hearing of it, he wept and told Huaiguang: "My father has achieved merit for the state; the son should be executed and cannot command troops."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Huaibin's son Chaocheng served in Huaiguang's army as commander of the right wing. When he heard the news he wept and told Huaiguang: "My father has served the state with merit. His son deserves execution and should not hold command."

sentences.zh: 懷光囚之。

translations.literal: Huaiguang imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang had him imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 於是游瑰屯邠寧，戴休顏屯奉天，駱元光屯昭應，尚可孤屯藍田，皆受李晟節度，晟軍聲大振。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yougui encamped at Binning; Dai Xiuyan at Fengtian; Luo Yuanguang at Zhaoying; Shang Ke'gu at Lantian—all under Li Sheng's command; Sheng's military prestige greatly revived.
translations.idiomatic: Yougui then held Binning; Dai Xiuyan Fengtian; Luo Yuanguang Zhaoying; Shang Ke'gu Lantian—all under Li Sheng's command. Sheng's prestige soared.

sentences.zh: 始，懷光方強，朱泚畏之，與懷光書，以兄事之，約分帝關中，永為鄰國。

translations.literal: At first Huaiguang was powerful; Zhu Ci feared him and wrote to him addressing him as elder brother, agreeing to divide the imperial capital in Guanzhong and be neighbors forever.
translations.idiomatic: At first, while Huaiguang was still strong, Zhu Ci feared him and wrote treating him as an elder brother, agreeing to divide the imperial domain in Guanzhong and remain neighbors forever.

sentences.zh: 及懷光決反，逼乘輿南幸，其下多叛之，勢益弱。

translations.literal: When Huaiguang resolved on rebellion and pressed the imperial carriage south, many of his subordinates rebelled against him and his power grew weaker.
translations.idiomatic: When Huaiguang turned rebel and drove the emperor south, many of his followers deserted him and his power waned.

sentences.zh: 泚乃賜懷光詔書，以臣禮待之，且征其兵。

translations.literal: Ci then granted Huaiguang an edict, treating him with the ritual of a subject, and also summoned his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Ci then sent Huaiguang an edict addressing him as a subject and demanded his troops.

sentences.zh: 懷光慚怒，內憂麾下為變，外恐李晟襲之，遂燒營東走，掠涇陽等十二縣，雞犬無遺。

translations.literal: Huaiguang was ashamed and angry, inwardly fearing mutiny among his command and outwardly fearing Li Sheng's attack; he burned his camp and fled east, plundering twelve counties including Jingyang—neither chicken nor dog was left.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang burned with shame and rage, fearing mutiny within and Li Sheng without. He burned his camp and fled east, ravaging twelve counties including Jingyang until neither fowl nor dog remained.

sentences.zh: 及富平，大將孟涉、段威勇將數千人奔於李晟，將士在道散亡相繼。

translations.literal: Reaching Fuping, Generals Meng She and Duan Weiyong led several thousand in flight to Li Sheng; officers and soldiers on the road scattered and fled continuously.
translations.idiomatic: At Fuping, Generals Meng She and Duan Weiyong defected to Li Sheng with several thousand men; along the march troops deserted in an unbroken stream.

sentences.zh: 至河中，或勸河中守將呂鳴岳焚橋拒之，鳴岳以兵少恐不能支，遂納之，河中尹李齊運棄城走。

translations.literal: Reaching Hedong, some urged the Hedong defending general Lü Mingyue to burn the bridge and resist; Mingyue feared his few troops could not hold out and admitted them; Hedong prefect Li Qiyun abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: At Hedong some urged the defending general Lü Mingyue to burn the bridge and hold him off, but Mingyue feared his small force could not resist and let him in; the prefect Li Qiyun abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 懷光遣其將趙貴先築壘於同州，刺史李紓懼，奔行在。

translations.literal: Huaiguang sent his general Zhao Guixian to build ramparts at Tongzhou; Prefect Li Shu was afraid and fled to the imperial camp.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang sent General Zhao Guixian to build fortifications at Tongzhou. Prefect Li Shu fled in terror to the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 幕僚裴向攝州事，詣貴先，責以逆順之理，貴先感寤，遂請降，同州由是獲全。

translations.literal: Staff member Pei Xiang took charge of the prefecture, went to Guixian, and rebuked him with the logic of rebellion versus loyalty; Guixian was moved to awakening and requested surrender; Tongzhou was thereby preserved whole.
translations.idiomatic: The staff officer Pei Xiang took charge of the prefecture, went to Guixian, and rebuked him with the rights and wrongs of loyalty and rebellion. Guixian was moved and offered to surrender; Tongzhou was saved intact.

sentences.zh: 向，遵慶之子也。

translations.literal: Xiang was the son of Zunqing.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xiang was the son of Pei Zunqing.

sentences.zh: 懷光使其將符嶠襲坊州，據之，渭北守將竇覦帥獵團七百圍之。

translations.literal: Huaiguang sent his general Fu Yao to raid Fangzhou and seize it; the Guanbei defending general Dou Gu led seven hundred hunter-soldiers to besiege him.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang sent General Fu Yao to seize Fangzhou. Dou Gu, the Guanbei defender, led seven hundred hunter-soldiers to besiege him.

sentences.zh: 嶠請降。

translations.literal: Yao requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yao asked to surrender.

sentences.zh: 詔以覦為渭北行軍司馬。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Gu as Guanbei campaign vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Dou Gu vice commander of the Guanbei campaign.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，以李晟兼京畿、渭北、鄜、坊、丹、延節度使。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Li Sheng was additionally made military commissioner of the Capital Region, Guanbei, Fu, Fang, Dan, and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai Li Sheng was also appointed military commissioner of the Capital Region, Guanbei, Fu, Fang, Dan, and Yan.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，車駕至城固。

translations.literal: On gengyin the imperial carriage reached Chenggu.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin the imperial carriage reached Chenggu.

sentences.zh: 唐安公主薨，上長女也。

translations.literal: Princess Tang'an died—she was the Emperor's eldest daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Tang'an died. She was the emperor's eldest daughter.

sentences.zh: 上在道，民有獻瓜果者，上欲以散試官授之，訪於陸贄，贄上奏，以為：「爵位恆宜慎惜，不可輕用。

translations.literal: On the road the Emperor wished to reward those who presented melons and fruit with probationary official titles; he consulted Lu Zhi; Zhi memorialized, holding that: "Ranks and titles should always be carefully cherished and must not be lightly used.
translations.idiomatic: On the march, commoners brought melons and fruit as gifts. The emperor wished to reward them with probationary official titles and asked Lu Zhi. Zhi memorialized: "Rank and office must always be guarded and must never be dispensed lightly.

sentences.zh: 起端雖微，流弊必大。

translations.literal: Though the beginning be slight, the harm that flows from it must be great.
translations.idiomatic: A small beginning can breed great harm.

sentences.zh: 獻瓜果者，止可賜之錢帛，不當酬以官。」

translations.literal: Those who present melons and fruit should only be given money and cloth—they must not be rewarded with office."
translations.idiomatic: Those who bring melons and fruit should receive only money and cloth, not office."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「試官虛名，無損於事。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Probationary offices are empty names—they harm nothing."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Probationary posts are empty titles. They do no harm."

sentences.zh: 贄又上奏，其略曰：「自兵興以來，財賦不足以供賜，而職官之賞興焉。

translations.literal: Zhi memorialized again, in summary: "Since the military uprising, funds have been insufficient for rewards, and the bounty of official posts has arisen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi memorialized again in substance: "Since the war began, the treasury has not had enough for rewards, and offices have been used as bounty instead.

sentences.zh: 青朱雜沓於胥徒，金紫普施於輿皁。

translations.literal: Azure and vermilion rank badges mixed among clerks; gold and purple broadly granted to carriage attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Azure and vermilion badges crowd the ranks of clerks; gold and purple sashes are handed out to carriage men.

sentences.zh: 當今所病，方在爵輕，設法貴之，猶恐不重，若又自棄，將何勸人！

translations.literal: Today's illness lies in ranks being too light; if we set laws to make them precious, we still fear they will not be valued—if we abandon them ourselves, with what shall we encourage people!
translations.idiomatic: Our trouble today is that rank has grown cheap. We strain to make it precious and still fear it is not honored enough—if Your Majesty now throws it away, how will you move anyone to serve!

sentences.zh: 夫誘人之方，惟名與利，名近虛而於教為重，利近實而於德為輕。

translations.literal: The means of enticing people are only fame and profit; fame is close to emptiness yet weighty in teaching, profit is close to substance yet light in virtue.
translations.idiomatic: There are only two ways to move men: fame and gain. Fame is near to emptiness yet heavy in moral teaching; gain is near to substance yet light in virtue.

sentences.zh: 專實利而不濟之以虛，則耗匱而物力不給。

translations.literal: To rely on substance alone without supporting it with emptiness exhausts stores and material goods cannot suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Rely on gain alone without balancing it with fame, and the treasury is drained until goods run out.

sentences.zh: 專虛名而不副之以實，則誕謾而人情不趨。

translations.literal: To rely on empty fame alone without supplementing it with substance is deceptive and popular feeling will not aspire.
translations.idiomatic: Rely on empty fame alone without real reward, and men see through the deceit and will not strive.

sentences.zh: 故國家命秩之制，有職事官，有散官，有勳官，有爵號，然掌務而授俸者，唯系職事之一官也，此所謂旋實利而寓虛名者也。

translations.literal: Therefore the state's system of ranks has office-holding posts, titular posts, merit posts, and noble titles—but only the office-holding post that manages duties and receives salary is substantive; this is what is called embodying real profit while lodging empty fame.
translations.idiomatic: The state therefore distinguishes office-holding posts, titular posts, merit posts, and noble titles—but only the office that carries duties and salary is substantive. That is how real gain is wrapped in empty fame.

sentences.zh: 其勳、散、爵號三者所繫，大抵止於服色、資廕而已，此所謂假虛名以佐實利者也。

translations.literal: The three categories—merit, titular, and noble titles—mostly concern only dress colors and qualification for hereditary privilege; this is what is called borrowing empty fame to assist real profit.
translations.idiomatic: Merit titles, titular ranks, and noble names mostly govern dress and hereditary privilege alone. That is how empty fame assists real gain.

sentences.zh: 今之員外、試官，頗同勳、散、爵號，雖則授無費祿，受不佔員，然而突銛鋒、排患難者則以是賞之，竭筋力、展勞效者又以是酬之。

translations.literal: Today's supernumerary and probationary offices largely resemble merit, titular, and noble titles; though they grant no salary and recipients do not fill quotas, yet those who charge through spear-points and brave hardships are rewarded with them, and those who exhaust sinew and show labor are also repaid with them.
translations.idiomatic: Today's supernumerary and probationary posts resemble merit titles, titular ranks, and noble names. They carry no salary and do not fill regular quotas, yet men who break the enemy line and brave danger receive them, and men who exhaust themselves in service are repaid with them.

sentences.zh: 若獻瓜果者亦授試官，則彼必相謂曰『吾以忘軀命而獲官，此以進瓜果而獲官，是乃國家以吾之軀命同於瓜果矣』。

translations.literal: If those who present melons are also given probationary office, they will surely say to one another: 'We obtained office by forgetting body and life, they obtained office by presenting melons and fruit—the state thus equates our bodies and lives with melons and fruit.'
translations.idiomatic: If melon-bearers also receive probationary office, soldiers will say to one another: 'We won rank by risking our lives; they won rank by bringing melons. The state has made our lives worth no more than fruit.'

sentences.zh: 視人如草木，誰復為用哉！

translations.literal: Regarding people as grass and trees—who will still be useful!
translations.idiomatic: Treat men like grass and wood, and who will still serve you willingly!

sentences.zh: 今陛下既未有實利以敦勸，又不重虛名而濫施，人無藉焉。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty has neither real profit to encourage with, nor esteems empty fame and lavishly grants it—people have nothing to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty now offers neither real reward to encourage service nor holds empty titles in esteem, yet dispenses them freely. Men have nothing to hold to.

sentences.zh: 則後之立功者，將曷用為賞哉！」

translations.literal: Then for those who achieve merit later—by what shall they be rewarded!"
translations.idiomatic: What reward will remain for those who earn merit hereafter!"

sentences.zh: 贄在翰林，為上所親信，居艱難中，雖有宰相，大小之事，上必與贄謀之，故當時謂之內相，上行止必與之俱。

translations.literal: Zhi was in the Hanlin Academy, trusted by the Emperor; in hardship though there were chancellors, great and small affairs the Emperor must discuss with Zhi; thus at the time he was called the inner chancellor; the Emperor's coming and going were always with him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi served in the Hanlin and was the emperor's closest adviser. Though chancellors held office, in hardship the emperor consulted Zhi on every matter great and small. Men called him the inner chancellor; the emperor would not travel without him.

sentences.zh: 梁、洋道險，嘗與贄相失，經夕不至，上驚憂涕泣，募得贄者賞千金。

translations.literal: The Liang and Yang routes were perilous; once he was separated from Zhi and did not arrive all night; the Emperor was alarmed, weeping, and offered a thousand gold reward for whoever found Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: The roads through Liang and Yang were treacherous. Once he lost Zhi for a whole night. The emperor wept in alarm and offered a thousand in gold to whoever brought him back.

sentences.zh: 久之，乃至，上喜甚，太子以下皆賀。

translations.literal: After a long while he arrived; the Emperor was overjoyed, and the Crown Prince down all congratulated.
translations.idiomatic: At last Zhi came. The emperor rejoiced, and from the crown prince down all offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 然贄數直諫，迕上意，盧杞雖貶官，上心庇之。

translations.literal: Yet Zhi repeatedly spoke frankly and offended the Emperor's intent; though Lu Qi was demoted, the Emperor's heart still shielded him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhi spoke frankly again and again and often crossed the emperor's wishes. Though Lu Qi had been demoted, the emperor still sheltered him in his heart.

sentences.zh: 贄極言杞奸邪致亂，上雖貌從，心頗不悅，故劉從一、姜公輔皆自下陳登用，贄恩遇雖隆，未得為相。

translations.literal: Zhi spoke forcefully that Qi was treacherous and caused chaos; though the Emperor outwardly assented, in heart he was quite displeased; thus Liu Congyi and Jiang Gongfu both rose from lower ranks to appointment, while Zhi's favor though lofty did not attain the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi insisted that Qi was treacherous and had brought on the rebellion. The emperor assented in appearance but was displeased at heart. Liu Congyi and Jiang Gongfu rose from humble posts to high office, while Zhi, for all his favor, never became chancellor.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，車駕至梁州。

translations.literal: On renchen the imperial carriage reached Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen the imperial carriage reached Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 山南地薄民貧，自安、史以來，盜賊攻剽，戶口減耗太半，雖節制十五州，租賦不及中原數縣。

translations.literal: Shannan was poor in land and people; since the An and Shi rebellions, bandits attacked and plundered, households reduced by more than half; though it administered fifteen prefectures, its tax levies did not equal several central plain counties.
translations.idiomatic: Shannan was thin soil and poor people. Since the An Lushan and Shi Siming rebellions, bandits had raided until more than half the households were gone. Though it governed fifteen prefectures, its tax yield did not match a few counties of the central plain.

sentences.zh: 及大駕駐蹕，糧用頗窘。

translations.literal: When the great carriage halted, food supplies were quite strained.
translations.idiomatic: When the court halted there, grain and supplies ran very short.

sentences.zh: 上欲西幸成都，嚴震言於上曰：「山南地接京畿，李晟方圖收復，借六軍以為聲援。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to go west to Chengdu; Yan Zhen spoke to the Emperor: "Shannan borders the capital region; Li Sheng is now planning recovery—borrow the Six Armies as vocal support.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to go west to Chengdu. Yan Zhen said to him: "Shannan borders the capital region. Li Sheng is fighting to recover Chang'an. He needs the Six Armies as his rear.

sentences.zh: 若幸西川，則晟未有收復之期也。」

translations.literal: If we go to the western circuit, Sheng will have no date for recovery."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty goes to the western circuit, Sheng will have no hope of recovery."

sentences.zh: 眾議未決，會李晟表至，言：「陛下駐蹕漢中，所以系億兆之心，成滅賊之勢。

translations.literal: The multitude had not decided when Li Sheng's memorial arrived, stating: "Your Majesty halting at Hanzhong binds the hearts of the hundred million and completes the momentum to destroy the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The court had not decided when Li Sheng's memorial arrived, saying: "Your Majesty's halt at Hanzhong holds the hearts of the empire and builds the momentum to destroy the rebels.

sentences.zh: 若規小舍大，遷都岷、峨，則士庶失望，雖有猛將謀臣，無所施矣！」

translations.literal: If we scheme small and abandon the large, moving the capital to Min and E, then gentry and common folk will lose hope; though there be fierce generals and shrewd ministers, nothing can be applied!"
translations.idiomatic: If you choose the lesser and abandon the greater, moving the capital to Min and E, gentry and commoners will lose heart. Though you have fierce generals and wise advisers, none of their plans can be used!"

sentences.zh: 上乃止。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 嚴震百方以聚財賦，民不至困窮而供億無乏。

translations.literal: Yan Zhen by every means gathered wealth and levies; the people did not reach destitution yet supplies for the court were not lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhen strained every device to gather revenue. The people did not sink into destitution, yet the court's needs were met.

sentences.zh: 牙將嚴礪，震之從祖弟也，震使掌轉餉，事甚修辦。

translations.literal: Military adjutant Yan Li was Zhen's paternal cousin's younger brother; Zhen had him manage transport of provisions; the matter was very well conducted.
translations.idiomatic: His military adjutant Yan Li, a younger cousin on his father's side, managed the transport of supplies and handled the work with great efficiency.

sentences.zh: 初，奉天圍既解，李楚琳遣使入貢，上不得已除鳳翔節度使，而心惡之。

translations.literal: At first, after the Fengtian siege was lifted, Li Chuilin sent envoys to present tribute; the Emperor had no choice but to appoint him military commissioner of Fengxiang, yet hated him in heart.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after the siege of Fengtian was lifted, Li Chuilin sent envoys with tribute. The emperor had no choice but to appoint him military commissioner of Fengxiang, though he loathed him.

sentences.zh: 議者言楚琳凶逆反覆，若不堤防，恐生窺伺。

translations.literal: Discussants said Chuilin was vicious and treacherous, duplicitous in rebellion—if not guarded against, he might covet and watch.
translations.idiomatic: Advisers said Chuilin was brutal, treacherous, and changeable in loyalty, and that if he were not watched he might seize his chance.

sentences.zh: 由是楚琳使者數輩至，上皆不引見，留之不遣。

translations.literal: Hence several envoys from Chuilin came; the Emperor would not receive any, detaining them without sending back.
translations.idiomatic: When several of Chuilin's envoys arrived, the emperor refused every audience and detained them without sending them home.

sentences.zh: 甫至漢中，欲以渾瑊代楚琳鎮鳳翔，陸贄上奏，以為：「楚琳殺帥助賊，其罪固大，但以乘輿未復，大憝猶存，勤王之師悉在畿內，急宣速告，晷刻是爭。

translations.literal: Just reaching Hanzhong, he wished to replace Chuilin at Fengxiang with Hun Jian; Lu Zhi memorialized, holding: "Though Chuilin's crime of killing his commander to aid the rebel is indeed great, yet while the imperial carriage is not yet restored and the great culprit still exists, the armies loyal to the throne are all within the capital region—urgent proclamations must race against time.
translations.idiomatic: Just after reaching Hanzhong, the emperor wished to replace Chuilin at Fengxiang with Hun Jian. Lu Zhi memorialized: "Chuilin's crime of murdering his commander to aid the rebels is grave, yet the throne is not restored, the chief rebel still lives, and the loyal armies are all in the capital region. Urgent orders must race against the clock.

sentences.zh: 商嶺則道迂且遙，駱谷復為盜所扼，僅通王命，唯在褒斜，此路若又阻艱，南北遂將□絕。

translations.literal: The Shangling route is circuitous and distant; the Luogu route is again blocked by bandits; barely imperial orders can pass—only through Baoxie; if this road too is obstructed, north and south will be cut off.
translations.idiomatic: The Shangling road is long and roundabout; the Luogu road is held by bandits. Imperial orders barely pass—only through Baoxie remains. If that road too is blocked, north and south will be severed.

sentences.zh: 以諸鎮危疑之勢，居二逆誘脅之中，洶洶群情，各懷向背。

translations.literal: In the perilous and doubtful situation of the various circuits, between two rebels' enticement and coercion, turbulent popular sentiment—each harbors inclinations this way and that.
translations.idiomatic: The circuits stand in peril and doubt, pressed between two rebels who entice and coerce them. Popular feeling runs high, and each man wavers between loyalty and defection.

sentences.zh: 倘或楚琳發憾，公肆猖狂，南塞要衝，東延巨猾，則我咽喉梗而心膂分矣。

translations.literal: If Chuilin should give vent to resentment and openly run riot, blocking the southern strategic throat and extending east to the great villain, then our throat would be choked and heart and spine divided.
translations.idiomatic: If Chuilin should give way to resentment and rise in open violence, blocking the southern passes and joining the great rebel in the east, our throat would be choked and our heart and spine torn apart.

sentences.zh: 今楚琳能兩端顧望，乃是天誘其衷，故通歸塗，將濟大業。

translations.literal: Now Chuilin can look both ways and hesitate—this is Heaven tempting his inmost heart, opening the road of return, about to aid the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Now Chuilin wavers between two sides. Heaven is turning his heart, clearing the road home, and he is ready to serve the great cause of restoration.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠宜深以為念，厚加撫循，得其持疑，便足集事。

translations.literal: Your Majesty truly ought deeply to bear this in mind, lavishly to soothe and guide him; gaining his suspended doubt is enough to gather the affair to success.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should take this deeply to heart, treat him generously, and win his wavering loyalty. That alone would be enough to settle the matter.

sentences.zh: 必欲精求素行，追抉宿疵，則是改過不足以補愆，自新不足以贖罪。

translations.literal: If one must minutely seek past conduct and dig out old flaws, then reforming faults is not enough to repair transgression, renewing oneself is not enough to redeem guilt.
translations.idiomatic: If you insist on probing every past deed and dredging up old faults, then no reform will ever atone for guilt and no repentance will ever redeem a crime.

sentences.zh: 凡今將吏，豈得盡無疵瑕，人皆省思，孰免疑畏！

translations.literal: Among all generals and officials today, how can none have blemishes? Each man reflects on himself—who escapes doubt and fear!
translations.idiomatic: Which of today's generals and officials is without blemish? Every man looks inward and asks who can escape doubt and fear.

sentences.zh: 又況阻命之輩，脅從之流，自知負恩，安敢歸化！

translations.literal: Moreover those who resisted orders, the stream coerced to follow, knowing themselves indebted in grace—how dare they return to allegiance!
translations.idiomatic: Still more those who defied orders and those dragged along by force know they have failed in grace. How would they dare come back?

sentences.zh: 斯釁非小，所宜速圖。

translations.literal: This breach is no small matter; it is fitting to plan for it swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: The harm is no small matter. Your Majesty should act on it at once.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下思英主大略，勿以小不忍虧撓興復之業也。」

translations.literal: I bow and wish Your Majesty to think on the great strategy of an enlightened ruler, not to let small impatience impair and shake the enterprise of restoration."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to keep the broad vision of a great ruler and not let a moment's resentment undermine the work of restoration."

sentences.zh: 上釋然開悟，善待楚琳使者，優詔存慰之。

translations.literal: The Emperor, relieved and enlightened, treated Chuilin's envoys well and with an excellent edict comforted and reassured them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger lifted. He treated Chuilin's envoys kindly and sent a gracious edict to comfort them.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，加宣武節度使劉洽同平章事。

translations.literal: On dingyou Liu Qia, military commissioner of Xuanwu, was made Associate Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou Liu Qia, military commissioner of Xuanwu, was appointed associate grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 己亥，以行在都知兵馬使渾瑊同平章事亦朔方節度使，朔方、邠寧、振武、永平、奉天行營兵馬副元帥。

translations.literal: On jihai Hun Jian, chief army controller at the mobile court, was made Associate Grand Councillor and also military commissioner of Shuofang, and deputy commander of the armies of Shuofang, Binning, Zhenwu, Yongping, and the Fengtian campaign.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai Hun Jian, chief army controller at the mobile court, was made associate grand councillor and military commissioner of Shuofang, and deputy commander over the armies of Shuofang, Binning, Zhenwu, Yongping, and the Fengtian campaign.

sentences.zh: 庚子，詔數李懷光罪惡，敘朔方將士忠順功名，猶以懷光舊勳，曲加容貸，其副元帥、太尉、中書令、河中尹並朔方等諸道節度、觀察等使，宜並罷免，授太子太保。

translations.literal: On gengzi an edict recounted Li Huaiguang's crimes and evils, narrated the loyal merit of Shuofang officers and soldiers, yet because of Huaiguang's old achievement bent to grant indulgence: his posts as deputy commander, Grand Marshal, Grand Secretariat Director, governor of Hezhong, and all military and surveillance commissioner posts in Shuofang and other circuits should together be removed, appointing him Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi an edict listed Li Huaiguang's crimes, praised the loyalty and merit of the Shuofang troops, yet in view of his past service showed leniency. He was stripped of his posts as deputy commander, grand marshal, director of the Secretariat, governor of Hezhong, and all his military and surveillance commissions, and was named grand guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 其所管兵馬，委本軍自舉一人功高望重者便宜統領，速具奏聞，當授旌旄，以從人欲。

translations.literal: The troops he commanded were entrusted to that army to choose on its own one man of lofty merit and heavy prestige to lead as expedient, quickly to memorialize for report; he would be granted the banner and staff to follow men's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: His troops were left to the army to choose a leader of high merit and standing, to report at once for appointment with banner and staff, following the soldiers' will.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，壬寅，以邠寧兵馬使韓游瑰為邠寧節度使。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on renyin Han Yougui, army controller of Binning, was made military commissioner of Binning.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, on renyin Han Yougui was appointed military commissioner of Binning.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，以奉天行營兵馬使戴休顏為奉天行營節度使。

translations.literal: On guimao Dai Xiuyan, army controller of the Fengtian campaign, was made military commissioner of the Fengtian campaign.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao Dai Xiuyan was appointed military commissioner of the Fengtian campaign.

sentences.zh: 靈武守將寧景璿為李懷光治第，另將李如暹曰：「李太尉逐天子，而景璿為之治第，是亦反也！」

translations.literal: Ning Jingxuan, defending general of Lingwu, built a mansion for Li Huaiguang; another general Li Ruxian said: "Grand Marshal Li drove out the Son of Heaven, yet Jingxuan builds him a mansion—this too is rebellion!"
translations.idiomatic: Ning Jingxuan, the defending general at Lingwu, was building a mansion for Li Huaiguang. Another general, Li Ruxian, said, "Grand Marshal Li drove out the Son of Heaven, and Jingxuan builds him a house. That is rebellion too!"

sentences.zh: 攻而殺之。

translations.literal: They attacked and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: They attacked and killed him.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，加李晟鄜坊、京畿、渭北、商華副元帥。

translations.literal: On jiachen Li Sheng was advanced to deputy commander of Yanfang, the capital region, Weibei, and Shanghua.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen Li Sheng was made deputy commander over Yanfang, the capital region, Weibei, and Shanghua.

sentences.zh: 晟家百口及神策軍士家屬皆在長安，朱泚善遇之。

translations.literal: Sheng's household of a hundred mouths and the Shence Army soldiers' families were all in Chang'an; Zhu Ci treated them well.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng's household of a hundred souls and the families of his Shence troops were all in Chang'an, and Zhu Ci treated them kindly.

sentences.zh: 軍中有言及家者，晟泣曰：「天子何在，敢言家乎！」

translations.literal: In the army when anyone spoke of family, Sheng wept and said: "Where is the Son of Heaven—how dare one speak of home!"
translations.idiomatic: When anyone in the army spoke of home, Sheng wept and said, "Where is the Son of Heaven? How dare you speak of family!"

sentences.zh: 泚使晟親近以家書遺晟曰：「公家無恙。」

translations.literal: Ci sent one of Sheng's intimates to present a family letter to Sheng, saying: "Your household is unharmed."
translations.idiomatic: Ci sent one of Sheng's close attendants with a letter from his family, saying, "Your household is safe."

sentences.zh: 晟怒曰：「爾敢為賊為間！」

translations.literal: Sheng in anger said: "You dare act as spy for the rebel!"
translations.idiomatic: Sheng raged, "You dare spy for the rebel!"

sentences.zh: 立斬之。

translations.literal: He was beheaded on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: He had him beheaded at once.

sentences.zh: 軍士未授春衣，盛夏猶衣裘褐，終無叛志。

translations.literal: The soldiers had not been issued spring garments; in high summer they still wore fur and coarse cloth, yet to the end had no thought of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The men had not received their spring clothing and in midsummer still wore furs and coarse cloth, yet never wavered in loyalty.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，以陝虢防遏使唐朝臣為河中、同終節度使。

translations.literal: On yisi Tang Zhaochen, defense commissioner of Shan-Guo, was made military commissioner of Hezhong, Tong, and Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi Tang Zhaochen was appointed military commissioner of Hezhong, Tong, and Zhong.

sentences.zh: 前河中尹李齊運為京兆尹，供晟軍糧役。

translations.literal: The former governor of Hezhong Li Qiyun was made governor of Jingzhao to supply Sheng's army with grain and labor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qiyun, former governor of Hezhong, was made governor of Jingzhao to provision Sheng's army with grain and labor.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，以魏博兵馬使田緒為魏博節度使。

translations.literal: On gengxu Tian Xu, army controller of Weibo, was made military commissioner of Weibo.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu Tian Xu was appointed military commissioner of Weibo.

sentences.zh: 渾瑊帥諸軍出斜谷，崔漢衡勸吐蕃出兵助之，尚結贊曰：「邠軍不出，將襲我後。」

translations.literal: Hun Jian led the armies out through Xié Valley; Cui Hanheng urged the Tibetans to send troops to aid him; Shang Jiezan said: "If the Bin army does not come out, they will strike our rear."
translations.idiomatic: Hun Jian led the armies out through Xié Valley. Cui Hanheng urged the Tibetans to send troops. Shang Jiezan said, "If the Binning army does not march out, they will strike us from behind."

sentences.zh: 韓游瑰聞之，遣其將曹子達將兵三千往會瑊軍，吐蕃遣其將論莽羅依將兵二萬從之。

translations.literal: Han Yougui heard this and sent his general Cao Zida with three thousand troops to join Jian's army; the Tibetans sent their general Lun Mangluoyi with twenty thousand to follow.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Yougui heard this, he sent Cao Zida with three thousand men to join Hun Jian. The Tibetans sent Lun Mangluoyi with twenty thousand in support.

sentences.zh: 李楚琳遣其將石鍠將卒七百從瑊拔武功。

translations.literal: Li Chuilin sent his general Shi Hong with seven hundred soldiers to follow Jian and capture Wugong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chuilin sent Shi Hong with seven hundred men to join Hun Jian and take Wugong.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，朱泚遣其將韓旻等攻武功，鍠以其眾迎降。

translations.literal: On gengxu Zhu Ci sent his generals Han Min and others to attack Wugong; Hong led his troops to welcome and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu Zhu Ci sent Han Min and others against Wugong. Hong brought his men over to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 瑊戰不利，收兵登西原。

translations.literal: Jian's battle went ill; he gathered his troops and ascended the western plateau.
translations.idiomatic: Hun Jian was beaten and withdrew his men to the western heights.

sentences.zh: 會曹子達以吐蕃至，擊旻，大破之於武亭川，斬首萬餘級，旻僅以身免。

translations.literal: Just then Cao Zida came with the Tibetans, struck Min, and routed him greatly at Wuting River, beheading more than ten thousand; Min barely escaped with his body.
translations.idiomatic: Then Cao Zida arrived with the Tibetans, struck Han Min, and routed him at Wuting River. More than ten thousand heads were taken. Min barely escaped alive.

sentences.zh: 瑊遂引兵屯奉天，與李晟東西相應，以逼長安。

translations.literal: Jian thereupon led his troops to encamp at Fengtian, coordinating east and west with Li Sheng to press Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Hun Jian then encamped at Fengtian, coordinating with Li Sheng from east and west to press Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 上欲為唐安公主造塔，厚葬之，諫議大夫、同平章事姜公輔表諫，以為「山南非久安之地，公主之葬，會歸上都，此宜儉薄，以副軍須之急。」

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to build a pagoda for Princess Tang'an and bury her richly; Remonstrance Counsellor and Associate Grand Councillor Jiang Gongfu memorialized in remonstrance, holding: "Shannan is not a place of long peace; the princess's burial will in time return to the upper capital—this ought to be spare and thin to match the army's urgent needs."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to build a pagoda for Princess Tang'an and give her a lavish burial. Jiang Gongfu, remonstrance counsellor and associate grand councillor, memorialized against it: "Shannan is no lasting home. The princess will one day be brought back to the capital. The burial should be modest to meet the army's urgent needs."

sentences.zh: 上使謂陸贄曰：「唐安造塔，其費甚微，非宰相所宜論。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent word to Lu Zhi: "Building a pagoda for Tang'an costs very little—it is not what a councillor ought to discuss.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent word to Lu Zhi: "The pagoda for Tang'an costs very little. It is not a matter for a councillor to debate.

sentences.zh: 公輔正欲指朕過失，自求名耳。

translations.literal: Gongfu simply wishes to point out my faults and seek fame for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Gongfu only wants to point out my faults and make a name for himself.

sentences.zh: 相負如此，當如何處之？」

translations.literal: A councillor who fails me thus—how should he be dealt with?"
translations.idiomatic: When a councillor fails me like this, what should be done with him?"

sentences.zh: 贄上奏，以為公輔任居宰相，遇事論諫，不當罪之，其略曰：「公輔頃與臣同在翰林，臣今據理辨直則涉於私黨之嫌，希旨順成則違於匡輔之義。

translations.literal: Zhi memorialized, holding that Gongfu's office was councillor, and when affairs arose to discuss and remonstrate he ought not be punished; the gist said: "Gongfu was lately with me in the Hanlin; if I now argue straight by principle I touch the suspicion of private faction, if I seek the intent and assent I violate the duty of aiding and correcting.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi memorialized that Gongfu, as councillor, had done his duty in remonstrance and should not be punished. He wrote in part: "Gongfu and I were lately together in the Hanlin. If I argue for him I risk the charge of faction. If I yield to Your Majesty's wish I betray the duty of a true minister.

sentences.zh: 涉嫌止貽於身患，違義實玷於群恩。

translations.literal: Avoiding suspicion only harms my own person; violating righteousness truly stains the grace of the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: To avoid suspicion would only spare my own skin. To violate righteousness would stain the grace shown to us all.

sentences.zh: 徇身忘君，臣之恥也！」

translations.literal: To indulge the body and forget the lord is a minister's shame!"
translations.idiomatic: To spare oneself and forget one's lord is a minister's shame!"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「唯暗惑之主，則怨讟溢於下國而耳不欲聞，腥德達於上天而心不求寤，迨乎顛覆，猶未知非。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Only a lord dark and deluded lets slander overflow the realm below yet will not hear it, lets foul virtue reach Heaven yet seeks no awakening—until overturn, still not knowing wrong."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Only a ruler blind and confused lets complaint flood the realm yet refuses to hear it, lets foul conduct reach Heaven yet will not wake—until ruin comes and he still does not know his error."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「當問理之是非，豈論事之大小！

translations.literal: He also said: "One should ask whether principle is right or wrong—how discuss whether the affair is large or small!
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "One should ask whether the principle is right or wrong, not whether the matter is large or small!

sentences.zh: 《虞書》曰：『兢兢業業，一日二日萬機。』

translations.literal: The Book of Yu says: 'Diligent, diligent—in one day, two days, ten thousand affairs.'
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Yu says, 'Be diligent, be diligent—in one day, two days, ten thousand affairs.'

sentences.zh: 唐、虞之際，主聖臣賢，慮事之微，日至萬數。

translations.literal: In the age of Tang and Yu, lord sage and ministers worthy, matters considered down to the minute reached ten thousand a day.
translations.idiomatic: In the age of Yao and Shun, though lord and ministers were sage and worthy, minute concerns still ran to ten thousand a day.

sentences.zh: 然則微之不可不重也，如此，陛下又安可忽而念乎！」

translations.literal: Thus what is minute must be heavily regarded—so how can Your Majesty lightly neglect and dismiss it!"
translations.idiomatic: If the minute could not be neglected then, how can Your Majesty dismiss it lightly now!"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「若以諫爭為指過，則剖心之主不宜見罪於哲王；

translations.literal: He also said: "If remonstrance is taken as pointing out faults, then the lord who laid open his heart should not have been faulted by the wise king;
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "If remonstrance is called fault-finding, then the lord who laid open his heart should not have been blamed by a wise king;

sentences.zh: 以諫爭為取名，則匪躬之臣不應垂訓於聖典。」

translations.literal: if remonstrance is taken as seeking fame, then the minister who gave not his body alone should not have been handed down as instruction in the sage canon."
translations.idiomatic: if remonstrance is called fame-seeking, then the minister who gave his life for his lord should not stand as a model in the sacred canon."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「假有意將指過，諫以取名，但能聞善而遷，見諫不逆，則所指者適足以彰陛下莫大之善，所取者適足以資陛下無疆之休。

translations.literal: He also said: "Suppose one truly meant to point out faults and remonstrate for fame—yet if one can hear good and change, see remonstrance and not resist, then what is pointed out will just suffice to display Your Majesty's immeasurable good, what is taken will just suffice to supply Your Majesty's boundless blessing.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Even if a minister meant to find fault and win fame, if Your Majesty hears good counsel and changes, welcomes remonstrance and does not resist, then what he points out will only display Your Majesty's great virtue, and what he gains will only add to Your Majesty's boundless blessing.

sentences.zh: 因而利焉，所獲多矣。

translations.literal: Profiting thereby, the gain is great.
translations.idiomatic: You would profit by it—and greatly.

sentences.zh: 儻或怒其指過而不改，則陛下招惡直之譏；

translations.literal: If perchance one is angry at the pointing out of faults and does not reform, then Your Majesty invites the reproach of hating the straight;
translations.idiomatic: But if you are angry at fault-finding and do not reform, Your Majesty will be blamed for hating honest counsel;

sentences.zh: 黜其取名而不容，則陛下被違諫之謗。

translations.literal: if one dismisses him for seeking fame and will not tolerate him, then Your Majesty bears the slander of rejecting remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: if you dismiss him for seeking fame and will not hear him, Your Majesty will be blamed for rejecting counsel.

sentences.zh: 是乃掩己過而過彌著，損彼名而名益彰。

translations.literal: This is to cover one's own faults yet faults become more manifest, to injure his fame yet fame grows brighter.
translations.idiomatic: You would hide your faults and make them more visible, wound his reputation and make it shine the brighter.

sentences.zh: 果而行之，所失大矣。」

translations.literal: If truly carried out, the loss is great."
translations.idiomatic: If you act on that course, the loss will be great."

sentences.zh: 上意猶怒，甲寅，罷公輔為左庶子。

translations.literal: The Emperor's mind was still angry; on jiayin Gongfu was removed to Left Subordinate of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor remained angry. On jiayin Jiang Gongfu was demoted to left subordinate of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 加西川節度使張延賞同平章事，賞其供億無乏故也。

translations.literal: Zhang Yanshang, military commissioner of Xichuan, was advanced to Associate Grand Councillor, rewarding that his provisioning had not fallen short.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yanshang, military commissioner of Xichuan, was made associate grand councillor in reward for keeping the court supplied without fail.

sentences.zh: 朱泚、姚令言數遣人誘涇原節度使馮河清，河清皆斬其使者。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci and Yao Lingyan repeatedly sent men to entice Feng Heqing, military commissioner of Jingyuan; Heqing beheaded every envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci and Yao Lingyan sent envoys again and again to win over Feng Heqing, military commissioner of Jingyuan. Heqing beheaded every one.

sentences.zh: 大將田希鑒密與泚通，殺河清，以軍府附於泚。

translations.literal: The great general Tian Xijian secretly communicated with Ci, killed Heqing, and attached the army headquarters to Ci.
translations.idiomatic: The senior general Tian Xijian secretly colluded with Zhu Ci, killed Heqing, and surrendered the command to the rebel.

sentences.zh: 泚以希鑒為涇原節度使。

translations.literal: Ci made Xijian military commissioner of Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci appointed Tian Xijian military commissioner of Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 上問陸贄：「近有卑官自山北來者，率非良士。

translations.literal: The Emperor asked Lu Zhi: "Lately low officials coming from north of the mountains are mostly not good men.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Lu Zhi: "Lately the minor officials arriving from north of the mountains have mostly not been trustworthy.

sentences.zh: 有刑建者，論說賊勢，語最張皇，察其事情，頗似窺覘，今已於一所安置。

translations.literal: There is one Xing Jian who discussed the rebel strength in the most exaggerated language; examining his conduct, it rather resembles spying—he has now been placed in one location under guard.
translations.idiomatic: One Xing Jian spoke of the rebels' strength in the most alarmist terms. His conduct looks like reconnaissance. I have already detained him in one place.

sentences.zh: 如此之類，更有數人，若不追尋，恐成奸計。

translations.literal: Men of this sort number several more; if not pursued and investigated, I fear they will complete a treacherous plot.
translations.idiomatic: There are several more like him. If they are not pursued, I fear a treacherous plot may succeed.

sentences.zh: 卿試思之，如何為更？」

translations.literal: Try to think—how might it be changed?"
translations.idiomatic: Consider what should be done instead."

sentences.zh: 贄上奏，以為今盜據宮闕，有冒涉險遠來赴行在者，當量加恩賞，豈得復猜慮拘囚！

translations.literal: Zhi memorialized, holding that now with bandits occupying the palace, those who brave danger from afar to reach the mobile court ought to be measured out added grace and reward—how can one again suspect, consider, and imprison!
translations.idiomatic: Zhi memorialized that while rebels hold the palace, those who brave danger to reach the mobile court should be rewarded generously. How can we suspect and imprison them again!

sentences.zh: 其略曰：「以一人之聽覽而欲窮宇宙之變態，以一人之防慮而欲勝億兆之奸欺，役智彌精，失道彌遠。

translations.literal: The gist said: "With one man's hearing and viewing to wish to exhaust the universe's transformations, with one man's guarding and considering to wish to overcome the hundred million's treachery and deceit—the more wit is deployed the finer, the further from the Way one goes.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote in part: "To try with one man's eyes and ears to master every change under heaven, and with one man's caution to defeat the deceit of millions—the cleverer the effort, the further from the Way.

sentences.zh: 項籍納秦降卒二十萬，慮其懷詐復叛，一舉而盡坑之，其於防虞，亦已甚矣。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu received two hundred thousand Qin surrendered soldiers, feared they harbored treachery and would rebel again, and in one move buried them all alive—his guarding and precaution were already extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu took in two hundred thousand Qin surrender troops, feared treachery, and buried them all alive at once. His caution could hardly have been greater.

sentences.zh: 漢高豁達大度，天下之士至者，納用不疑，其於備慮，可謂疏矣。

translations.literal: Gaozu of Han was open and magnanimous; when men of talent under heaven came, he received and used them without doubt—his preparation and caution can be called loose.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu of Han was open and magnanimous. When talent came to him from all the realm, he employed it without suspicion. His caution could hardly have been looser.

sentences.zh: 然而項氏以滅，劉氏以昌，蓄疑之與推誠，其效固不同也。

translations.literal: Yet the Xiang clan perished and the Liu clan flourished—hoarding suspicion and extending sincerity, their effects are surely not the same.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the house of Xiang was destroyed and the house of Liu rose. Hoarding suspicion and extending sincerity yield very different ends.

sentences.zh: 秦皇嚴肅雄猜，而荊軻奮其陰計；

translations.literal: The First Emperor of Qin was stern, fierce, and suspicious, yet Jing Ke roused his hidden plot;
translations.idiomatic: The First Emperor of Qin was stern and deeply suspicious, yet Jing Ke carried out his secret plot;

sentences.zh: 光武寬容博厚，而馬援輸其款誠。

translations.literal: Emperor Guangwu was tolerant, broad, and thick, and Ma Yuan offered his sincere allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu was tolerant and generous, and Ma Yuan gave him his whole-hearted loyalty.

sentences.zh: 豈不以虛懷待人，人亦思附；

translations.literal: Is it not that with empty breast one treats others, and others also think to attach?
translations.idiomatic: Is it not because an open heart wins men, and men in turn wish to serve?

sentences.zh: 任數御物，物終不親！

translations.literal: to rely on schemes to control things—things in the end do not draw near!
translations.idiomatic: While to rule by schemes alone leaves nothing truly loyal!

sentences.zh: 情思附則感而悅之，雖寇億化為心膂矣；

translations.literal: when feeling thinks to attach, one is moved and delights them—even enemies transform into heart and spine;
translations.idiomatic: When men feel welcome they are moved to devotion, and even enemies become loyal followers;

sentences.zh: 意不親則懼而阻之，雖骨肉結為億慝矣。」

translations.literal: when intent is not close, one fears and obstructs them—even bone and flesh knot into a hundred million evils."
translations.idiomatic: when they feel rejected they fear and resist, and even kin become countless enemies."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「陛下智出庶物，有輕待人臣之心；

translations.literal: He also said: "Your Majesty's wisdom surpasses the multitude, and there is a heart that lightly treats ministers;
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Your Majesty's wisdom surpasses all others, yet there is a tendency to slight your ministers;

sentences.zh: 思周萬機，有獨馭區寓之意；

translations.literal: thought encompasses ten thousand affairs, and there is intent to drive the realm alone;
translations.idiomatic: your thought embraces every affair, and there is a wish to rule the realm alone;

sentences.zh: 謀吞眾略，有過慎之防；

translations.literal: plans swallow the multitude of strategies, and there is a guard of excessive caution;
translations.idiomatic: your plans swallow every scheme, and there is a guard of excessive caution;

sentences.zh: 明照群情，有先事之察；

translations.literal: brightness illuminates the feelings of the mass, and there is foresight before events;
translations.idiomatic: your clarity reads every mood, and there is foresight before events;

sentences.zh: 嚴束百辟，有任刑致理之規；

translations.literal: strictly binding the hundred officials, there is a rule of relying on punishment to bring order;
translations.idiomatic: you bind the hundred officials strictly, trusting punishment to bring order;

sentences.zh: 威制四方，有以力勝殘之志。

translations.literal: awe controls the four quarters, and there is will to overcome the cruel by force.
translations.idiomatic: you awe the four quarters, with a will to overcome cruelty by force alone.

sentences.zh: 由是才能者怨於不任，忠藎者憂於見疑，著勳業者懼於不容，懷反側者迫於及討，馴致離叛，構成禍災。

translations.literal: Hence the able resented not being employed, the loyal and earnest grieved at being suspected, those with shining merit feared not being tolerated, those harboring wavering were pressed toward punishment—gradually leading to separation and rebellion, composing disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the able resented being unused, the loyal grieved at suspicion, men of merit feared rejection, and the wavering were driven toward rebellion—until separation and disaster followed.

sentences.zh: 天子所作，天下式瞻，小猶慎之，矧又非小！

translations.literal: What the Son of Heaven does, the realm under heaven takes as model—even small matters demand caution, how much more when they are not small!
translations.idiomatic: What the Son of Heaven does, the realm watches as its model. Even small acts demand caution—how much more these!

sentences.zh: 願陛下以覆車之轍為戒，實宗社無疆之休。」

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to take the overturned cart's track as warning—truly the boundless blessing of altar and state."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to take the wreck of past carts as warning, for the boundless blessing of the dynasty."

sentences.zh: 丁巳，以前山南東道節度使南皮賈耽為工部尚書。

translations.literal: On dingsi Jia Dan of Nanpi, former military commissioner of Shannan East Circuit, was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi Jia Dan of Nanpi, former military commissioner of Shannan East Circuit, was appointed minister of works.

sentences.zh: 先是，耽使行軍司馬樊澤奏事行在。

translations.literal: Earlier Dan had sent his campaign army marshal Fan Ze to memorialize at the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Jia Dan had sent his campaign army marshal Fan Ze to report at the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 澤既覆命，方大宴，有急牒至，以澤代耽為節度使。

translations.literal: Ze had just returned his report and they were at a great banquet when an urgent dispatch arrived appointing Ze to replace Dan as military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ze had just reported back and a great banquet was under way when an urgent dispatch arrived appointing him to replace Jia Dan as military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 耽內牒懷中，宴飲如故，顏色不改。

translations.literal: Dan hid the dispatch inside his robe, feasted and drank as before, his countenance unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Dan slipped the dispatch into his robe, drank on as before, and never changed color.

sentences.zh: 宴罷，召澤告之，且命將吏謁澤。

translations.literal: When the banquet ended he summoned Ze and told him, and ordered the generals and officials to pay court to Ze.
translations.idiomatic: When the feast ended he summoned Fan Ze, told him the news, and ordered his officers to pay their respects to the new commissioner.

sentences.zh: 牙將張獻甫怒曰：「行軍為尚書問天子起居，乃敢自圖節金戊，奪尚書土地，事人不忠，眾心不服，請殺之。」

translations.literal: Military adjutant Zhang Xianfu in anger said: "The campaign marshal came for the Minister to inquire after the Son of Heaven's health, yet dared to scheme for himself the commander's insignia, seize the Minister's territory—serving one's lord without loyalty, the multitude's hearts will not submit; I ask to kill him."
translations.idiomatic: His military adjutant Zhang Xianfu raged: "The campaign marshal was sent to inquire after the Son of Heaven's health for the minister, yet he dared scheme for the commission himself and seize the minister's territory. That is disloyal service. The men will not accept it. I ask leave to kill him."

sentences.zh: 耽曰：「是何言也！

translations.literal: Dan said: "What words are these!
translations.idiomatic: Jia Dan said, "What talk is this!

sentences.zh: 天子所命，即為節度使矣！」

translations.literal: What the Son of Heaven commands—that man is already military commissioner!"
translations.idiomatic: Whom the Son of Heaven appoints is already military commissioner!"

sentences.zh: 即日離鎮，以獻甫自隨，軍府遂安。

translations.literal: That same day he left the command, taking Xianfu with him, and the army headquarters was thereafter at peace.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he left the post, taking Zhang Xianfu with him, and the headquarters settled into peace.

sentences.zh: 左僕射李揆自吐蕃還，甲子，薨於鳳州。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director Li Kui, returning from Tibet, on jiazi died at Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kui, left vice director, returning from Tibet, died at Fengzhou on jiazi.

sentences.zh: 韓游瑰引兵會渾瑊於奉天。

translations.literal: Han Yougui led his troops to join Hun Jian at Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yougui led his troops to join Hun Jian at Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，加平盧節度使李納同平章事。

translations.literal: On bingyin Li Na, military commissioner of Pinglu, was advanced to Associate Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin Li Na, military commissioner of Pinglu, was made associate grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，義王泚薨。

translations.literal: On dingmao Prince of Yi Zhu Ci died.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao Zhu Ci, Prince of Yi, died.

sentences.zh: 朱滔攻貝州百餘日，馬寔攻魏州亦逾四旬，皆不能下。

translations.literal: Zhu Tao attacked Beizhou for more than a hundred days; Ma Shi attacked Weizhou also for more than forty days—neither could take them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao besieged Beizhou for more than a hundred days, and Ma Shi besieged Weizhou for more than forty. Neither could take the city.

sentences.zh: 賈林復為李抱真說李武俊曰：「朱滔志吞貝、魏，復值田悅被害，儻旬日不救，則魏博皆為滔有矣，魏博既下，則張孝忠必為之臣。

translations.literal: Jia Lin again spoke for Li Baozhen to Li Wujun, saying: "Zhu Tao's ambition is to swallow Bei and Wei; moreover Tian Yue has been killed—if in ten days or so there is no rescue, then all Weibo will belong to Tao; once Weibo falls, Zhang Xiaozhong will surely become his subject.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Lin again spoke for Li Baozhen to Li Wujun: "Zhu Tao aims to swallow Bei and Wei. Tian Yue has just been killed. If no relief comes within ten days, all of Weibo will fall to Tao. Once Weibo falls, Zhang Xiaozhong will surely submit to him.

sentences.zh: 滔連三道之兵，益以回紇，進臨常山，明公欲保其宗族，得乎！

translations.literal: Tao will link the armies of three circuits, add the Uyghurs, advance to press Changshan—can Your Illustriousness preserve your clan?
translations.idiomatic: Tao will unite three circuits' armies, add the Uyghurs, and march on Changshan. Can you preserve your clan then?

sentences.zh: 常山不守，則昭義退保西山，河朔盡入於滔矣。

translations.literal: If Changshan is not held, then Zhaoyi will withdraw to guard the western mountains, and all Hebei will enter Tao's possession.
translations.idiomatic: If Changshan falls, Zhaoyi will retreat to the western mountains, and all Hebei will pass to Zhu Tao.

sentences.zh: 不若乘貝、魏未下，與昭義合兵救之。

translations.literal: Better to strike while Bei and Wei have not yet fallen and unite troops with Zhaoyi to rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: Better to act while Bei and Wei still hold out and join Zhaoyi in a relief army.

sentences.zh: 滔既破亡，則關中喪氣，朱泚不日梟夷，鑾輿反正，諸將之功，孰有居明公之右者哉！」

translations.literal: Once Tao is broken and destroyed, Guanzhong will lose its spirit; Zhu Ci will soon be executed; the imperial carriage will return to the right path—among the generals' achievements, who will stand above Your Excellency!"
translations.idiomatic: Once Tao is destroyed, Guanzhong will lose heart; Zhu Ci will soon be executed; the throne will return to order—and among the generals, who will rank above you!"

sentences.zh: 武俊悅，從之。

translations.literal: Wujun was pleased and followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun was pleased and agreed.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，武俊軍於南宮東南，抱真自臨洺引兵會之，與武俊營相拒十里。

translations.literal: On the day wuchen, Wujun encamped southeast of Nangong; Baozhen led troops from Linming to join him, their camps facing each other ten li apart.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuchen day, Wujun encamped southeast of Nangong; Baozhen marched from Linming to join him, their camps ten li apart.

sentences.zh: 兩軍尚相疑，明日，抱真以數騎詣武俊營，賓客共諫止之，抱真命行軍司馬盧玄卿勒兵以俟，曰：「吾之此舉，系天下安危，若其不還，領軍事以聽朝命亦惟子，勵將士以雪仇恥亦惟子。」

translations.literal: The two armies still mistrusted each other; the next day Baozhen rode with a few horsemen to Wujun's camp. His guests all urged him to stop, but Baozhen ordered his field marshal Lu Xuanqing to hold the troops in readiness and said, "My going concerns the safety of the realm; if I do not return, take command and obey the court's orders—that is yours alone; rouse the officers and men to avenge this shame—that too is yours alone."
translations.idiomatic: The two armies still distrusted each other; the next day Baozhen rode to Wujun's camp with only a few horsemen. His staff urged him to stop, but he ordered his field marshal Lu Xuanqing to hold the troops ready and said, "This ride concerns the fate of the realm. If I do not return, take command and obey the court—that is yours; rouse the men to vengeance—that is yours as well."

sentences.zh: 言終，遂行。

translations.literal: When he had finished speaking, he went.
translations.idiomatic: He finished and rode on.

sentences.zh: 武俊嚴備以待之，抱真見武俊，敘國家禍難，天子播遷，持武俊哭，流涕縱橫。

translations.literal: Wujun made strict preparations to receive him; when Baozhen met Wujun he spoke of the state's calamity and the Son of Heaven's exile, seized Wujun and wept, tears streaming in every direction.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun received him under strict guard; Baozhen spoke of the realm's disaster and the emperor's exile, seized Wujun, and wept until tears ran down his face.

sentences.zh: 武俊亦悲不自勝，左右莫能仰視。

translations.literal: Wujun too was overcome with grief; those beside him could not bear to look up.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun too was overcome with grief; those around him could not bear to look up.

sentences.zh: 遂與武俊約為兄弟，誓同滅賊。

translations.literal: He then pledged brotherhood with Wujun and swore to destroy the rebels together.
translations.idiomatic: He pledged brotherhood with Wujun and swore to destroy the rebels together.

sentences.zh: 武俊曰：「相公十兄名高四海，曏蒙開諭，得棄逆從順，免菹醢之罪，享王公之榮。

translations.literal: Wujun said, "Your Excellency, my elder brother of the covenant, your fame fills the four seas; I was once enlightened by your counsel and able to abandon rebellion for loyalty, escape the punishment of being minced alive, and enjoy the honors of prince and duke.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun said, "Your fame fills the four seas, Elder Brother; you once opened my eyes and let me turn from rebellion to loyalty, escape execution, and enjoy princely honors.

sentences.zh: 今又不間胡虜，辱為兄弟，武俊當何以為報乎！

translations.literal: Now, without regard for barbarian or Chinese, you deign to be my brother—how can Wujun repay you!
translations.idiomatic: Now you set aside the difference between us and Chinese and deign to be my brother—how can I ever repay you!

sentences.zh: 滔所恃者回紇耳，不足畏也。

translations.literal: What Tao relies on is only the Uyghurs—they are not worth fearing.
translations.idiomatic: Tao relies only on the Uyghurs—they are nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 戰日，願十兄按轡臨視，武俊決為十兄破之。」

translations.literal: On the day of battle, I ask my elder brother to hold his reins and watch from above; Wujun will surely break them for you."
translations.idiomatic: On the day of battle, I ask you to hold your reins and watch; I will break them for you."

sentences.zh: 抱真退入武俊帳中，酣寢久之。

translations.literal: Baozhen withdrew into Wujun's tent and slept soundly for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhen withdrew into Wujun's tent and slept deeply for a long while.

sentences.zh: 武俊感激，待之益恭，指心仰天曰：「此身已許十兄死矣！」

translations.literal: Wujun was deeply moved, treated him with still greater respect, pointed to his heart and looked to heaven, saying, "This body is already pledged to die for my elder brother!"
translations.idiomatic: Wujun was deeply moved and treated him with still greater respect; pointing to his heart he looked to heaven and said, "This life is already pledged to die for you!"

sentences.zh: 遂連營而進。

translations.literal: They then joined camps and advanced together.
translations.idiomatic: They then united their camps and advanced together.

sentences.zh: 山南地熱，上以軍士未有春服，亦自御夾衣。

translations.literal: Shannan was hot; because the soldiers had no spring clothing, the emperor himself wore layered garments.
translations.idiomatic: Shannan was hot; because the soldiers lacked spring clothing, the emperor himself wore layered garments.
